Non ci chiese come stavamo. Non ci disse.easy: He did not ask how we were. He did not tell us what it was like on the other side. He just dictated: formulae, tables, drawings explained point by point. It was the last part of his Masterwork, the part death had not let him finish. At the end of the third night the needle stopped, went back to the middle and wrote one last sentence: *"Now leave me in peace."*
Non ci chiese come stavamo. Non ci disse.short: He asked nothing: he dictated the last part of his Masterwork. Then the needle tapped: *"Now leave me in peace."*

Lo abbiamo fatto. Il Masterwork è finito.easy: We did. The Masterwork is finished, Doctor, and it was published with his name. The Telegraph is taken apart, in the attic. We have never switched it on again.
Lo abbiamo fatto. Il Masterwork è finito.short: The Masterwork was published. The Telegraph is in the attic, dismantled.

Egregio dottore, la Chiesa ha vinto, e n.easy: Dear Doctor, the Church won, and it was not a gentle victory. The bishop came to {0} in the spring of 1906 with a decree, two policemen and a list of names. Our family's name was first.
Egregio dottore, la Chiesa ha vinto, e n.short: Dear Doctor, the Church won. The bishop came in 1906 with a list of names, and ours was first.

La sede del Circolo bruciò la notte di P.easy: The Circle's building burned on the night of Pentecost. Somehow the fire crossed the road and reached the estate. The greenhouses, the cages, the laboratory and the volumes of the Journal burned. The Telegraph, as it melted, made a noise the firemen described as a cry of pain.
La sede del Circolo bruciò la notte di P.short: At Pentecost the Circle burned, and the fire reached the estate. The Telegraph melted with a wail.

Sulle ceneri il vescovo ha fatto costrui.easy: On the ashes the bishop had a chapel built for the souls in purgatory. I go there every Sunday, like everyone. The priest says its walls are the quietest in the diocese, and he is right: no one ever knocks there.
Sulle ceneri il vescovo ha fatto costrui.short: A chapel now stands on the ashes. Its walls are the quietest in the diocese.

Ma nella cripta, sotto l'altare, dove un.easy: But in the crypt, under the altar, where the laboratory used to be, the sexton has not gone down for years.

Egregio dottore, lei mi chiede chi gover.easy: Dear Doctor, you ask me who is in charge in {0}. On paper, the town council, and a mayor who is still called Bódi. In reality, since that night in 1905, every decision goes first across a little table.
Egregio dottore, lei mi chiede chi gover.short: Dear Doctor, the council governs {0}. But since 1905 every decision passes first across a little table.

La Grande Seduta finì con la nostra fami.easy: The Great Séance ended with our family leading the Circle of the Last Hour, and the Circle welcomed us like an heir it had waited for a long time. The undertaker's, the bank, the newspaper, the school: everything is ours, or belongs to someone who owes us a favour. The widows bless us. And, people say, so do the dead.
La Grande Seduta finì con la nostra fami.short: We lead the Circle, and everything is ours or owes us a favour. The widows bless us, and so do the dead.

Non creda che sia un potere comodo. Ogni.easy: Do not think it is a comfortable power. Every Thursday evening we ask advice from those who came before us, and the dead are difficult advisers: they forget nothing, forgive nothing, and have all the time in the world.
Non creda che sia un potere comodo. Ogni.short: But the dead are demanding counsellors: they forget nothing, forgive nothing, and have all the time in the world.

Le scrivo con il loro permesso. Mi hanno.easy: I am writing with their permission. They asked me to tell you that your work has been noticed, and that, whenever you want, there will be a chair for you too at our table. I advise you not to want it.
Le scrivo con il loro permesso. Mi hanno.short: They ask me to tell you there is a chair for you at our table. I advise you not to want it.

Caro dottore, la riconosco dalla calligr.easy: Dear Doctor, I recognise you by your handwriting. You, however, will not recognise mine: it is not the handwriting of the person who signs this letter. Since the night of the Great Séance, when the vial broke in the hands of {0}, this hand has written for me.
Caro dottore, la riconosco dalla calligr.short: Dear Doctor, you will not recognise my hand. Since the vial broke in the hands of {0}, this hand has written for me.

Mi presento, anche se forse ha già capit.easy: Let me introduce myself, though perhaps you have already understood: Eszter Vámos, consoler. For fifty years they called me a cheat, a witch, a prophet, a saint. They were all a little right. The secret of eternal life, Doctor, was not for sale: it was in that vial. I only had to find the right person, mad enough to let me in.
Mi presento, anche se forse ha già capit.short: I am Eszter Vámos, consoler. The secret of eternal life was in that vial: I only needed someone mad enough to let me in.

Questo corpo è più giovane del mio, e ha.easy: This body is younger than mine and has warmer hands: I use it carefully. I am writing to you because you are reading my records, and I have always liked people who read me carefully.
Questo corpo è più giovane del mio, e ha.short: This body is young, and I use it with care. I write because you read my minutes so attentively.

Ho cercato a lungo un erede vivente da i.easy: I looked for a long time for a living heir to question, as I did for the other documents in the file. I did not find one. The papers end on the night of 31 December 1905, in the middle of a record: the veil was torn, and the family voted not to cross it. Then, says the last line, "the fog came in through the windows".
Ho cercato a lungo un erede vivente da i.short: I found no living heir. The papers stop on 31 December 1905: the veil was torn, the family did not cross it, and "the fog came in through the windows".

Dal 1906 {0} non compare più sulle carte.easy: Since 1906 {0} is no longer on any map. Trains do not stop there, the telegraph does not answer, and travellers who try to get there say they walked for hours in a white fog, around a cemetery, before finding themselves back where they started.
Dal 1906 {0} non compare più sulle carte.short: Since 1906 {0} has vanished from the maps. Those who try to reach it walk for hours in the fog, around a cemetery, and end up where they began.

Mi chiederete, allora, dove ho trovato q.easy: So you will ask me where I found these crates. I ask myself too. I remember the evening train, the umbrella, the kind and very tired priest. I do not remember how I left the village.
Mi chiederete, allora, dove ho trovato q.short: Where did I find these crates? I remember the train, the umbrella, the priest. I do not remember leaving the village.

Scrivo dal mio studio di Budapest. Dalla.easy: I am writing from my study in Budapest. For three days I have seen only fog from the window. And someone, politely, is knocking.

Alla tenuta, quella notte, i colpi alle.easy: That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is softer than usual. Almost shy.

Nella nebbia non sei mai senza compagnia.easy: In the fog you are never without company. A light step follows you, always three metres behind, and stops when you stop. The lanterns lean towards you like flowers towards the sun, and the estate dog will not sleep in your room any more. In the village they say you carry the Presences with you, the way other people carry a smell.
Nella nebbia non sei mai senza compagnia.short: In the fog a light step always follows you. The village says you carry the Presences with you.

Una mattina, sulla soglia, trovi un rega.easy: One morning, on the doorstep, you find a gift wrapped in a sheet wet with fog. Better not to ask where it came from.
Una mattina, sulla soglia, trovi un rega.short: On the doorstep you find a gift in a wet sheet. Better not to ask where it came from.

La Gazzetta ha pubblicato la tua fotogra.easy: The Gazette has printed your photograph in an article about "families who talk to the dead", and since then everyone in town knows you. Ladies cross the street, the tram conductors let you ride free, children follow you singing a rhyme about the veil. At night, under the window, there are bare footprints on the wet cobbles.
La Gazzetta ha pubblicato la tua fotogra.short: Since your photo in the Gazette, the whole town knows you. At night there are bare footprints under your window.

Una mattina, sulla soglia, trovi un rega.easy: One morning, on the doorstep, you find a gift with a note: *"From the one who watches you."*
Una mattina, sulla soglia, trovi un rega.short: On the doorstep, a gift: *"From the one who watches you."*

In laboratorio, sotto la lampada, il reg.easy: In the laboratory, under the lamp, the gift turns out to be useful, and just as unsettling as you thought. You say thank you aloud, to be polite. Someone behind the door seems pleased.
In laboratorio, sotto la lampada, il reg.short: The gift is useful, and unsettling. You say thank you. Someone behind the door is pleased.

Lo seppellisci in un angolo del cimitero.easy: You bury it in a corner of the cemetery, at night, with a prayer you half remember. The next morning the footprints under the window are gone. In their place, on the sill, there is a smooth white pebble, like the ones children leave on graves.
Lo seppellisci in un angolo del cimitero.short: You bury it at night. Next day the footprints are gone, and a white pebble sits on the sill.

Le voci arrivano con la nebbia, e con la.easy: The voices come with the fog, and they do not leave. They speak German, Hungarian, a country tongue nobody uses any more. A woman asks you every evening if you have seen her son; a soldier asks you the way to a village that burned forty years ago. Some voices you know: you heard them at the table as a child, when the grown-ups thought you were asleep.
Le voci arrivano con la nebbia, e con la.short: With the fog come the voices, and they stay. Some you know: you heard them at the table as a child.

Le senti nel ronzio dei fili della luce,.easy: You hear them in the hum of the electric wires, in the train whistle, in the needle of the café phonograph when the record has ended and spins on empty. Hundreds of voices, thousands, polite and patient like a crowd in a waiting room. Each one waits its turn to tell you something. Some, it seems to you, have waited fifty years.
Le senti nel ronzio dei fili della luce,.short: You hear voices in the wires, the train, the phonograph. Thousands of them, patient. Each wants to tell you something.

Scaldi la cera di una candela tra le dit.easy: You warm candle wax between your fingers and fill your ears with it, like the sailors in the story. The silence is so sudden that your head spins. For three days you hear nothing: not the voices, not the rain, not the people talking to you at table. On the fourth day you take the wax out, and the voices are gone. For now.
Scaldi la cera di una candela tra le dit.short: You stop your ears with wax. After three days of silence, the voices are gone. For now.

Il secondo volume del Journal ha una pag.easy: The second volume of the Journal has an extra page. It was not there yesterday: you know because you counted them all the evening before. It is written in two hands, your grandfather's and your parent's, one line each, like a conversation. The formula at the bottom is wrong in one place only.
Il secondo volume del Journal ha una pag.short: There is a new page in the Journal, written by your grandfather and your parent. The formula has a single mistake.

Tra le pagine del Journal, che ormai son.easy: Among the pages of the Journal, which now fill three and a half volumes, there is a sheet typed on the Telegraph's bone keys: you know it by the slightly crooked letters. No one has switched the machine on. The sheet describes an experiment, carefully and impatiently, and it has only one mistake.
Tra le pagine del Journal, che ormai son.short: In the Journal is a sheet typed by the Telegraph, though no one switched it on. The experiment has a single mistake.

La pagina brucia male, a scatti, come ca.easy: The page burns badly, in fits and starts, like damp paper. When it is ash, a torn margin is left in the Journal with three words written crosswise: *"Pity. Another time."* But by now you have worked out the right formula yourself.
La pagina brucia male, a scatti, come ca.short: You burn it. On the torn margin is written: *"Pity. Another time."* But you have worked out the right formula.

Le signore del Circolo ti salutano per n.easy: The ladies of the Circle greet you by name, the important people give you their seat at the café, the village doctor writes about you to a colleague in Vienna. A few days later a black-edged card arrives: an invitation "to a dinner among people who will not give up, in the fog, as in the old days". In the envelope, as a courtesy, there is some money.
Le signore del Circolo ti salutano per n.short: Everyone knows you. A black-edged card arrives: an invitation to dinner, and some money.

Il giornale di Budapest ti dedica un tra.easy: The Budapest newspaper writes about you, with a drawing that does not look much like you. In town people ask you for autographs, advice, a good word with the dead. A few days later a black-edged card arrives: an invitation "to a dinner among people who will not give up, like your family for three generations". In the envelope, as a courtesy, there is some money.
Il giornale di Budapest ti dedica un tra.short: The Budapest paper writes about you. A black-edged card arrives: an invitation to dinner, and some money.

La cena è in una casa con le persiane ch.easy: The dinner is in a house with closed shutters, by candlelight. The guests are kind, well dressed, and eat nothing. No one asks you to sign anything; they only ask about your family, fondly, the way one asks about distant relatives. As you leave you notice that each guest has an empty place laid beside them.
La cena è in una casa con le persiane ch.short: The guests are kind and eat nothing. Each has an empty place laid beside them.

Rimandi la busta al mittente, senza un b.easy: You send the envelope back without a note, the seal unbroken. The next day it comes back to you, also unopened, with one line on the back: *"The place stays laid."* The village says you turned down the Circle, and someone shakes your hand in the street.
Rimandi la busta al mittente, senza un b.short: You send it back. It returns: *"The place stays laid."*

La proposta cade nel silenzio come un cu.easy: The suggestion falls into the silence like a spoon on the floor. Then someone nods, and someone else shrugs. Father Anzelm comes that same afternoon, blesses every room, even the laboratory cages, and leaves looking like someone who has patched a coat that will not last.
La proposta cade nel silenzio come un cu.short: Father Anzelm blesses every room, but leaves looking as if he knows it will not be enough.

La proposta piace più di quanto ti aspet.easy: The idea goes down better than you thought: after all you are scientists, or a scientist's children. In one afternoon Father's bedroom becomes an observatory: a pendulum clock, a notebook with columns for the hour, the knocks and the wall, a silk thread from one wall to the other with three little bells. That night all three ring, in the right order.
La proposta piace più di quanto ti aspet.short: Father's room becomes an observatory, with a thread and three bells. That night all three ring.

Parli del tempo, delle strade, del prezz.easy: You talk about the weather, the roads, the price of firewood. The others follow you, relieved. It is a long, polite, completely useless conversation; and by the end of breakfast everyone knows, without saying so, that tonight no one will blow out the candle.
Parli del tempo, delle strade, del prezz.short: You talk about the weather. But everyone knows no one will blow out the candle tonight.

La terra sulla tomba del padre è ancora.easy: The earth on Father's grave is still fresh. From the middle of the mound comes a brass tube as thick as a wrist, closed with a screw cap, with a little bell on top. The gravedigger, a big, quiet man called Mihály, takes off his cap before he explains.
La terra sulla tomba del padre è ancora.short: A brass tube with a bell comes out of Father's grave. Mihály the gravedigger explains.

\"Istruzioni del defunto\", dice. \"Scri.easy: "The dead man's instructions," he says. "Written by him and paid to the notary in advance. The tube goes down to the coffin, level with his mouth. If the gentleman wakes, he can call; if he has no breath, there is the bell cord, tied to his wrist. It must stay open forty days. Then it can be closed." He puts his cap back on. "I have buried many gentlemen who were afraid of being buried alive. This is the first who seemed afraid of the opposite."
\"Istruzioni del defunto\", dice. \"Scri.short: "If the gentleman wakes, he can call up the tube or ring the bell. It stays open forty days. This one seemed afraid of the opposite of being buried alive."

Il cimitero di notte è più piccolo che d.easy: At night the cemetery seems smaller: the graves crowd together, the low wall comes closer. You unscrew the cap and kneel in the mud. Cold air rises from the tube, smelling of wax and earth. At first you hear nothing; then, far down, three very faint knocks, like a fingernail on wood. One. Two. One.
Il cimitero di notte è più piccolo che d.short: At night you open the tube. From deep down come three faint knocks. One. Two. One.

Poi una voce, così bassa che potrebbe es.easy: Then a voice, so low it could be the wind in the brass, says one word that you do not understand. You screw the cap back on with shaking hands. When you stand up there is a drop of dew on the bell that does not fall.
Poi una voce, così bassa che potrebbe es.short: Then a voice says a word you do not understand. You close the tube with shaking hands.

Il fabbro cola il piombo nel tubo davant.easy: The smith pours the lead into the tube in front of you and Father Anzelm, who wanted to be there and blesses it the way one blesses a bell. The molten metal goes down gurgling, then stops, and for a moment a long hiss comes out of the tube, like someone holding their breath. The smith says it is the air. The priest says nothing.
Il fabbro cola il piombo nel tubo davant.short: The smith seals the tube with lead. A long hiss comes out of it. The priest says nothing.

Il campanello lo togli tu, e lo porti a.easy: You take the bell off yourself and carry it home in a handkerchief. You put it in a drawer of your desk. All winter it never rings; and all winter you open the drawer every evening to check.
Il campanello lo togli tu, e lo porti a.short: You keep the bell in a drawer. It never rings, but you check every evening.

Lasci il tubo aperto, come voleva il pad.easy: You leave the tube open, as Father wanted, and give Mihály a coin to check the bell every morning. For thirty-nine days the gravedigger comes to the estate, takes off his cap and says: "Nothing."
Lasci il tubo aperto, come voleva il pad.short: You leave the tube open. For thirty-nine days Mihály comes to say: "Nothing."

Il quarantesimo giorno non viene. Lo tro.easy: On the fortieth day he does not come. You find him at the cemetery, sitting on the grave, pale. The bell has not rung, he says. But last night, for the first time, someone unscrewed the cap from the inside. Then, to thank you for your patience, he quietly offers you a favour of the trade: something from the common grave that no one will come looking for.
Il quarantesimo giorno non viene. Lo tro.short: On the fortieth day, the cap has been unscrewed from inside. Mihály offers you something from the common grave.

Nella bottega del fabbro, mentre aspetti.easy: At the smithy, while you wait for your horse to be shod, you hear a rhythm you know. It comes from behind the forge: one knock, two, one. A pause. Then again: one, two, one. Behind the forge is a boy of six or seven, with singed hair and a little hammer, patiently tapping on the side of the anvil.
Nella bottega del fabbro, mentre aspetti.short: At the smithy you hear a rhythm you know: one, two, one. A little boy is beating it on the anvil.

Si chiama Jóska, ed è il figlio del fabb.easy: His name is Jóska, and he is the smith's son. He explains, very seriously, that at night in bed he hears knocking from across the river, from the big house, and that he answers, so the one knocking does not feel alone. His father takes him by the ear and says sorry: the boy has too much imagination, and the big house, with respect, makes too much noise.
Si chiama Jóska, ed è il figlio del fabb.short: Jóska, the smith's son, says that at night he answers the knocking from the big house, so it won't feel alone.

Jóska ti insegna il gioco con l'aria imp.easy: Jóska teaches you the game with the important air of a teacher. One knock is yes, two is no, but everyone knows that; the best part, he says, is that if you wait long enough the knocks become letters, and the letters words. He shows you his: a row of notches on the door, counted night after night.
Jóska ti insegna il gioco con l'aria imp.short: Jóska teaches you that, with patience, knocks become letters and words. He shows you the notches on his door.

Quando te ne vai ti chiede se tornerai..easy: When you leave he asks if you will come back. You say yes. His father, touched, fills your pockets with bits of metal he no longer needs.
Quando te ne vai ti chiede se tornerai..short: You promise to come back. His father gives you scraps of metal.

Il fabbro toglie il martelletto al figli.easy: The smith takes the hammer from his son and sends him inside with a cuff on the ear. The boy does not cry. He stops in the doorway and looks at you for a long time, dry-eyed, as if he wants to remember you.
Il fabbro toglie il martelletto al figli.short: The smith sends the boy indoors. He does not cry, and looks at you as if to remember you.

Il fabbro, mortificato, non vuole essere.easy: The smith, embarrassed, will not take money for the horse. That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is louder and faster than usual, like someone knocking with no one answering.
Il fabbro, mortificato, non vuole essere.short: That night the knocking at the estate is louder, like someone knocking with no answer.

Madame Vámos è in paese, a consolare una.easy: Madame Vámos is in the village, comforting a widow. Her caravan is standing at the edge of the wood, the horses grazing and the door ajar, as if someone had left it open on purpose. Inside it is dark, and it smells of incense, of horse, and of something sweeter, like flowers left too long in water.
Madame Vámos è in paese, a consolare una.short: Madame is in the village. Her caravan door is ajar, as if left open on purpose.

Ci sono un tavolino rotondo coperto da u.easy: There is a round table covered in velvet, four chairs, a portrait turned to the wall and, under the bunk, a trunk with iron corners. No one sees you. You have time to look at one thing, maybe two.
Ci sono un tavolino rotondo coperto da u.short: Inside are a table and a trunk. You have time to look at one thing.

Sotto il drappo il tavolino ha una gamba.easy: Under the cloth the table has a single hollow leg, with a wooden lever just sticking out of the floor: a pedal, right where the foot of whoever sits in the medium's chair would be. And from the top a very fine black silk thread hangs down and disappears through a hole in the floor.
Sotto il drappo il tavolino ha una gamba.short: Under the table is a pedal, and a black silk thread that vanishes into the floor.

È un trucco, ed è un trucco ben fatto. L.easy: It is a trick, and a good one. You are still admiring it when the table, though no one has touched the pedal, knocks once on the floor. You run out of the caravan. But at home you draw the mechanism from memory.
È un trucco, ed è un trucco ben fatto. L.short: It is a trick. But the table knocks once by itself, and you flee. At home you draw the mechanism.

Il baule non è chiuso a chiave. Dentro c.easy: The trunk is not locked. Inside are shawls, packs of cards, a phial of phosphorus and a bundle of letters tied with a black ribbon. You know the handwriting at once: it is the Journal's. They are letters from your father to *"Eszter"*, dated from 1821 to a few months ago.
Il baule non è chiuso a chiave. Dentro c.short: In the trunk are letters from your father to *"Eszter"*, from 1821 to a few months ago.

Ne leggi una sola, la prima che ti capit.easy: You read only one, the first you find: it speaks of an experiment, a door, and a promise: "we shall see each other again, one way or another". It is dated three weeks after the funeral. You put everything back, the ribbon tied as before, and for days you cannot think of anything else.
Ne leggi una sola, la prima che ti capit.short: One letter promises: "we shall see each other again, one way or another". It is dated after the funeral.

Chiudi la porta del carro e ti allontani.easy: You close the caravan door and leave. On the path you meet Madame Vámos, coming back from the village with her basket on her arm. She looks at your hand, the one that closed the door, and smiles.
Chiudi la porta del carro e ti allontani.short: You leave. On the path you meet Madame, who looks at your hand and smiles.

\"Siete una persona educata\", dice. \"V.easy: "You are a polite person," she says. "Your father, at your age, was not." Then she puts in your hand a very old silver coin, with a face you do not know, "for when you want to come back". You cannot tell if it is a compliment or a down payment.
\"Siete una persona educata\", dice. \"V.short: "You are polite. Your father was not." She gives you an old coin, "for when you want to come back".

Nell'ufficio del notaio, al primo piano.easy: In the notary's office, on the first floor of the Town Hall, it smells of damp paper and tobacco. The notary is a small man with a slightly crooked wig, and he looks like someone who has to read something he would rather not have found. It is an addition to Father's will, in his own hand, which came by post from Vienna a week after the funeral.
Nell'ufficio del notaio, al primo piano.short: The notary reads an addition to Father's will, which came from Vienna a week after the funeral.

*\"La mia camera resti com'è: il letto,.easy: *"Let my room stay as it is: the bed, the papers, the lamp, the chair by the bed. Let nothing be moved and the window not be opened as long as someone, in that room, keeps knocking. After that, do as you like."* The notary looks up from the page. "The law does not make you," he says. "But in your place I would think about it."
*\"La mia camera resti com'è: il letto,.short: *"Let my room stay as it is as long as someone there keeps knocking."* "The law does not make you," says the notary. "But I would think about it."

La camera resta com'era: il letto con la.easy: The room stays as it was: the bed with the shape of the body, the lamp out, the chair by the bed, always pulled out a little, as if someone had just sat in it. The housekeeper will not dust it. You go in now and then, in the evening, and each time the chair is closer to the bed.
La camera resta com'era: il letto con la.short: The room stays as it was. Each time you go in, the chair is closer to the bed.

Fai portare via tutto in un pomeriggio:.easy: You have it all taken away in one afternoon: the bed to the attic, the papers to the study, the chair to the kitchen. Under the mattress there are dozens of folded sheets, full of notes, with the dates of Father's last nights. At the bottom of the last one is a line bigger than the rest: *"They answer."*
Fai portare via tutto in un pomeriggio:.short: Under the mattress are the notes of Father's last nights. The last line says: *"They answer."*

Quella notte, nella camera vuota, nessun.easy: That night, in the empty room, no one knocks. They knock in the kitchen, against the chair.
Quella notte, nella camera vuota, nessun.short: That night they knock in the kitchen, against the chair.

Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di cavo.easy: At the Farmer's Market, among the baskets of cabbages, a travelling photographer has a stand with a black cloth and a box of silver plates. His name is Koch, he comes from Pest, and he takes portraits of the living and the dead: the dead cost more, he says, because they keep still better, but they must be propped up with an iron rod behind the back.
Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di cavo.short: At the market the photographer Koch takes portraits of the living and the dead. The dead cost more.

Quando sente il tuo cognome si illumina..easy: When he hears your surname his face lights up. Three months before the funeral, he says, he took a portrait of your father at the estate, and was never paid. He shows you the plate: Father sitting, thin, with the Journal on his knees and an empty chair beside him. And in the silver, if you tilt it to the light, on the empty chair sits a woman in a black shawl.
Quando sente il tuo cognome si illumina..short: Koch has a portrait of your father, never paid for. Tilt the plate, and on the empty chair beside him sits a woman in a black shawl.

Paghi il debito di tuo padre, con gli in.easy: You pay your father's debt, with interest, and take the portrait home wrapped in a cloth. You hang it in the study. By day the chair beside Father is empty. In the evening, with the lamp lit, not always.
Paghi il debito di tuo padre, con gli in.short: You hang the portrait in the study. By day the chair is empty. In the evening, not always.

Il fotografo si gratta la testa. Nella s.easy: The photographer scratches his head. There was no woman in the room, he says: only himself, the gentleman, and the empty chair, which the gentleman insisted on having beside him, "for a friend who will come". The pose took two minutes. Halfway through, the gentleman smiled. That is why his mouth is a little blurred in the portrait.
Il fotografo si gratta la testa. Nella s.short: "There was no woman," says Koch. "The gentleman wanted the empty chair, for a friend who would come. Halfway through the pose he smiled."

Il fotografo esita, poi strofina la last.easy: The photographer hesitates, then wipes the plate with a rag soaked in cyanide, in front of you. The silver clouds over, Father vanishes, the chair vanishes. The woman vanishes last, and it seems to you, though it must be the light, that she has time to turn towards you.
Il fotografo esita, poi strofina la last.short: The plate is wiped clean. The woman vanishes last, and seems to turn towards you.

Il becchino del cimitero, interrogato da.easy: The cemetery's gravedigger, questioned by this newspaper, confirms that at night someone from the estate goes to listen at the brass tube coming out of the old man's grave. He does not say what can be heard. He says that, since then, the bell no longer needs the wind.
Il becchino del cimitero, interrogato da.short: The gravedigger confirms: at night someone from the estate listens at the tube. And the bell rings without wind.

Il fabbro, che ha colato il piombo nel t.easy: The smith, who poured the lead into the tube of the old man's grave in front of the reverend, says he heard the metal whistle like a kettle. The reverend has asked him not to tell anyone.
Il fabbro, che ha colato il piombo nel t.short: The smith says the lead in the tube whistled like a kettle.

Si segnala inoltre che il figlio del fab.easy: It is also reported that the smith's son, a boy of six, is going round the village teaching everyone a new game: knocking on walls in a certain order. Mothers are asked to keep an eye on their children.
Si segnala inoltre che il figlio del fab.short: The smith's son is teaching everyone to knock on walls. Mothers are asked to watch their children.

Qualcuno sostiene che sotto il tavolino.easy: Some say there is a pedal under the caravan table. Madame Vámos, when asked, invited whoever says so to sit in her place and try.
Qualcuno sostiene che sotto il tavolino.short: Some talk of a pedal under the table. Madame invites them to try it.

La famiglia della tenuta va a messa al c.easy: The family from the estate goes to Mass all together, in the front row, in their best clothes and with the faces of people who have not slept. Father Anzelm, from the pulpit, stares at them for a while and changes the end of his sermon: he talks about the prodigal son. The ladies in black, at the back of the church, look at each other.
La famiglia della tenuta va a messa al c.short: You go to Mass in the front row. Father Anzelm changes his sermon to the prodigal son.

La domenica mattina, mentre le campane s.easy: On Sunday morning, while the bells ring, the family from the estate opens the gate. The ladies in black come up two by two, veils lowered, and sit in the big drawing room, under Father's portrait, to talk about their dead. None of you does anything special: you just listen. The ladies leave at lunchtime, comforted. That Sunday Father Anzelm preaches to half a church.
La domenica mattina, mentre le campane s.short: You open the gate to the widows and listen to them talk of their dead. That Sunday the church is half empty.

La Bank di {0} è una stanza sola, con un.easy: The Bank of {0} is a single room, with a brass grille, a safe as big as a wardrobe and a banker, Mr Weisz, who wears his sleeve protectors even on Sundays. He receives you awkwardly, like someone who has news to give and does not know if it is good.
La Bank di {0} è una stanza sola, con un.short: Mr Weisz the banker receives you awkwardly: he has news for you.

Il conto di tuo padre, spiega, non si è.easy: Your father's account, he explains, did not close when he died. For twenty years, on the first of each month, the same deposit has come from Vienna, signed only with three initials: **C. U. O.** It came this month too. "As if the sender," says Mr Weisz, straightening his glasses, "did not know. Or did not care."
Il conto di tuo padre, spiega, non si è.short: For twenty years a monthly deposit signed **C. U. O.** has come into your father's account. It came this month too.

Il signor Weisz conta le banconote due v.easy: Mr Weisz counts the notes twice, with wet fingers, and gives them to you in an envelope. That evening, as you empty the envelope onto the laboratory table, out falls a note the banker swears he never saw. A single line, in an elegant, old-fashioned hand: *"For the family's expenses. There are always expenses, in a family."*
Il signor Weisz conta le banconote due v.short: In the envelope is a note: *"For the family's expenses. There are always expenses, in a family."*

Firmi l'ordine di restituzione, e il sig.easy: You sign the order to send it back, and Mr Weisz sends it to Vienna by Thursday's coach. On the first of the next month the deposit arrives on time, doubled, with a note: *"We insist."*
Firmi l'ordine di restituzione, e il sig.short: You send it back. Next month it returns, doubled: *"We insist."*

Lo fai restituire di nuovo. La voce gira.easy: You send it back again. Word gets round, as all word does in {0}: the family from the estate refuses money, and in the village anyone who refuses money is either a saint or has something to hide.
Lo fai restituire di nuovo. La voce gira.short: You send it back again. The village says whoever refuses money is a saint or has something to hide.

Il signor Weisz esita, poi apre il regis.easy: Mr Weisz hesitates, then opens the ledger. Beside each deposit, in place of a signature, there is a small ink drawing: a carnation, carefully blacked in. Under the first one, from 1828, there is also a full name: *O. Garai*.
Il signor Weisz esita, poi apre il regis.short: Instead of a signature there is always a black carnation. Under the first, from 1828, is a name: *O. Garai*.

L'ultimo versamento, quello di questo me.easy: This month's deposit has the same drawing and the same name, in the same handwriting, pressed with the same force. "A son, I imagine," says the banker. "Or a grandson. Good families pass their signature down, like the silver."
L'ultimo versamento, quello di questo me.short: This month's deposit has the identical signature. "A son, or a grandson," says the banker.

Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di uova.easy: At the Farmer's Market, among the baskets of eggs and the chicken cages, a woman in black catches you by the sleeve. It is Panna Kovács, the miller's widow. Her husband died of cholera last summer, in three days, without being able to say where he had hidden thirty years of savings; and she, with four children and the mill standing still, sells eggs to buy bread.
Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di uova.short: Panna Kovács, the miller's widow, stops you at the market. Her husband died without saying where he hid his savings.

\"Voi parlate con i morti\", ti dice, se.easy: "You talk to the dead," she says, without lowering her voice. "The whole village knows it. Madame wants a florin a séance, and I haven't got a florin. You ask him where the money is. He'll answer you: you're educated people."
\"Voi parlate con i morti\", ti dice, se.short: "You talk to the dead. Madame wants a florin, and I haven't got one. You ask him where the money is."

La porti dietro il banco del pane, le pr.easy: You take her behind the bread stall, hold her hands and close your eyes, as you have seen Madame do. After a while you say the first thing that comes into your head: behind the stove, a loose brick. The widow kisses your hands and runs to the mill.
La porti dietro il banco del pane, le pr.short: You fake a séance and say the first thing that comes to mind: behind the stove, a loose brick. The widow runs to the mill.

Torna la sera, coperta di fuliggine: die.easy: She comes back in the evening, covered in soot: there was nothing behind the stove. But she is not angry. She says her husband trusted no one, not even dead, but that she, for the first time in months, has slept. The next day the village says the family from the estate comforts widows for free.
Torna la sera, coperta di fuliggine: die.short: There was nothing behind the stove. But the widow, for the first time in months, has slept.

Madame Vámos accetta il tuo fiorino senz.easy: Madame Vámos takes your florin without looking at it. The séance is short: the medium is silent for a long time, then speaks in a hoarse man's voice and says to count the paddles of the wheel, from the left, up to the seventh.
Madame Vámos accetta il tuo fiorino senz.short: Madame takes the florin. In a man's voice she says: count the paddles of the wheel to the seventh.

Sotto la settima pala, in una scatola di.easy: Under the seventh paddle, in a tin box wedged between the boards, are the miller's savings, down to the last kreuzer. The widow cries, laughs, and swears that from Sunday she will go to the Thursday séances instead of Mass. You wonder how Madame knew; and whether she knew before you paid her.
Sotto la settima pala, in una scatola di.short: Under the seventh paddle are the savings. You wonder how Madame knew, and since when.

Le dici che no, non sai parlare con i mo.easy: You tell her that no, you cannot talk to the dead, and that anyone who swears they can usually wants a florin. The widow is silent for a moment. Then she thanks you: in the whole village you are the first person who has promised her nothing.
Le dici che no, non sai parlare con i mo.short: You tell her the truth. She thanks you: you are the first who has promised her nothing.

Prima di andarsene ti mette tra le bracc.easy: Before she goes she puts her best hen into your arms, flapping and protesting. Refusing it would be an insult; and in the laboratory, as everyone knows, an animal always comes in handy.
Prima di andarsene ti mette tra le bracc.short: She gives you her best hen. In the laboratory an animal always comes in handy.

**DISGRAZIA ALLO STAGNO.** Domenica pome.easy: **TRAGEDY AT THE POND.** On Sunday afternoon little Péter Szűcs, called Peti, eight years old, the cooper's son, fell through the ice of the park pond, where he was playing with other children although it was forbidden. The body was found only yesterday, after three days of searching.
**DISGRAZIA ALLO STAGNO.** Domenica pome.short: **TRAGEDY AT THE POND.** Peti, aged eight, the cooper's son, fell through the ice of the pond. He was found after three days.

Chi lo ha visto racconta un fatto singol.easy: Those who saw him tell of something strange: the boy did not look drowned, but asleep, with pink cheeks and lips slightly open. The doctor says it was the cold. The mother will not let him be buried. Madame Vámos has offered to watch over him for a whole night. The cooper, they say, has debts, and the family from the estate buys bodies for its studies.
Chi lo ha visto racconta un fatto singol.short: Peti looks asleep. His mother will not bury him, Madame wants to watch over him, and the estate buys bodies for its studies.

Paghi una bara bianca, una lapide piccol.easy: You pay for a white coffin, a small headstone with an angel and a meal for the village after the Mass. Father Anzelm says Mass with shining eyes. Peti's mother does not thank you: she speaks to no one. But the next day, on the estate doorstep, you find a basket of apples wrapped in straw, with no note.
Paghi una bara bianca, una lapide piccol.short: You pay for Peti's funeral. His mother speaks to no one, but the next day she leaves you a basket of apples.

Il bottaio accetta il denaro senza guard.easy: The cooper takes the money without looking you in the eye. The body comes to the estate at night, on a cart covered with sacks. In the laboratory you examine it for a long time, by lamplight: no water in the lungs, no sign of a struggle, the heart stopped like a clock no one has wound.
Il bottaio accetta il denaro senza guard.short: The cooper sells the body. In the laboratory you find Peti did not drown: his heart simply stopped.

Prendi appunti per tutta la notte. All'a.easy: You take notes all night. At dawn, when you look up from your notebook, it seems to you that the child's eyelids have moved. Not yours: his. You close the notebook, and do not open it again for a month.
Prendi appunti per tutta la notte. All'a.short: At dawn the child's eyelids seem to have moved. You close your notebook for a month.

Madame Vámos veglia il bambino nella bot.easy: Madame Vámos watches over the child in the cooper's workshop, among the staves and iron hoops, with one candle. You stay in the doorway, because someone from the family must be there: she asked for it.
Madame Vámos veglia il bambino nella bot.short: Madame watches over the child. You stay in the doorway: she wanted someone from the family.

Verso le tre la medium si china sul picc.easy: Around three the medium bends over the small body, speaks into its ear, and listens. Then she turns to the mother and tells her that Peti is cold, but not afraid, and that he will play with the other children again, when the fog comes. The next day they bury him. At the funeral the mother smiles.
Verso le tre la medium si china sul picc.short: Madame tells the mother that Peti will play with the other children again, when the fog comes. At the funeral the mother smiles.

Al Builder's Office ti aspetta un giovan.easy: At the Builder's Office a young clerk is waiting for you, with a black carnation in his buttonhole and a leather folder under his arm. He represents, he says, "a society of wealthy and discreet people" who want to buy your family's strip of land between the cemetery and the main road: a field of nettles where the gravedigger's goats graze.
Al Builder's Office ti aspetta un giovan.short: A young man with a black carnation wants to buy your field by the cemetery.

Il prezzo che offre è il doppio di quant.easy: He offers twice what it is worth, and three times what anyone in {0} has ever paid for a field of nettles. The foreman, behind him, signals with his whole face for you to accept.
Il prezzo che offre è il doppio di quant.short: He offers twice what it is worth. The foreman signals you to accept.

Firmi, e il giovane ti paga in monete d'.easy: You sign, and the young man pays you in gold coins, counted one by one onto a black silk handkerchief. The gravedigger's goats are moved the next day. For years nothing is built on the field; but now and then, at night, someone walks there with a lantern, pacing out the distance from the graves.
Firmi, e il giovane ti paga in monete d'.short: You sell. For years nothing is built, but at night someone paces out the field.

Il giovane non insiste. Ripone la cartel.easy: The young man does not insist. He puts his folder away, wishes you good day and leaves. A week later the society buys the land on the other side of the cemetery, at the price of a field of nettles. The foreman looks at you as if you had turned down a dowry.
Il giovane non insiste. Ripone la cartel.short: You refuse. The society buys the land on the other side of the cemetery.

Il giovane esita, poi apre la cartella e.easy: The young man hesitates, then opens the folder and shows you a drawing: a low, elegant building with a bell tower but no bell; from the tower dozens of thin wires run down, taut as harp strings, to the graves, one by one. "A house of rest," he says. "For the living, of course."
Il giovane esita, poi apre la cartella e.short: The drawing shows a building with a bell tower but no bell, and many wires stretched to the graves.

Non vendi. Ma il disegno, a casa, lo cop.easy: You do not sell. But at home you copy the drawing from memory, and draw it three times before you understand what the wires are for.
Non vendi. Ma il disegno, a casa, lo cop.short: You do not sell. At home you copy the drawing, and work out what the wires are for.

Il fabbro ti prende da parte, vicino all.easy: The smith takes you aside, near the forge, like someone getting something off his chest. Last summer, just before Father died, an elegant gentleman with a black carnation ordered copies of all the estate's keys from him: the gate, the front door, the study, the cellar, even the writing desk. He brought the wax moulds ready-made.
Il fabbro ti prende da parte, vicino all.short: Before Father died, a gentleman with a black carnation had copies made of all the estate's keys.

\"La cosa strana\", dice il fabbro, abba.easy: "The strange thing," says the smith quietly, "is that the moulds were brought to me by your father himself, the day before. He put them in my hand and said: when a gentleman with a black flower comes for them, give them to him. It is all paid for."
\"La cosa strana\", dice il fabbro, abba.short: "Your father brought me the moulds himself," says the smith. "He said to give them to the gentleman with the black flower."

Dietro la forgia, Jóska ascolta tutto co.easy: Behind the forge, Jóska listens to it all wide-eyed, and gives you a nod, as between partners in crime.
Dietro la forgia, Jóska ascolta tutto co.short: Jóska hears it all, and gives you a knowing nod.

Il fabbro cambia tutte le serrature in u.easy: The smith changes all the locks in a week, and for a few nights the estate seems quieter. Then one morning you find the study door open, the new key in the lock from the inside, and the Journal on the desk open at the last page, the one with the sentence underlined twice.
Il fabbro cambia tutte le serrature in u.short: You change the locks. But one morning the study is open from the inside, and the Journal lies open at the last page.

Il fabbro conserva gli stampi di tutti i.easy: The smith keeps the moulds of all his customers, the Circle's too. For a few coins he makes you a copy: a long, dark key with an eye cut into the handle. It opens a door at the back of the house on the square. One night you use it: behind the door are some stairs, a cellar and, against the wall, a padded little hammer hanging from a rope.
Il fabbro conserva gli stampi di tutti i.short: With the copied key you get into the Circle's cellar at night. Against the wall hangs a padded little hammer on a rope.

Lasci le cose come sono. Il signore con.easy: You leave things as they are. The gentleman with the carnation never comes, at least not by day. But one night you hear the gate open, then the front door, then the study door, one after another, unhurried, with the right keys. In the morning nothing is missing. On the desk is a black carnation.
Lasci le cose come sono. Il signore con.short: One night you hear every door open, one after another. In the morning there is a black carnation on the desk.

La famiglia, intanto, ha cominciato a ri.easy: Meanwhile the family has started to collect the money from Vienna every month. No one talks about it at table. But from then on the unsigned letters come more often, and are more affectionate.
La famiglia, intanto, ha cominciato a ri.short: The family collects the money from Vienna. The unsigned letters come more often, and more fondly.

La famiglia, intanto, continua a rimanda.easy: Meanwhile the family keeps sending the money back to Vienna each month, and each month it comes back, doubled. From then on the unsigned letters sound offended, like those of a neglected aunt.
La famiglia, intanto, continua a rimanda.short: The family sends the money back, and it returns doubled. The unsigned letters sound offended.

Al mercato, la vedova del mugnaio raccon.easy: At the market, the miller's widow tells anyone who will listen about the savings found under the seventh paddle, and who took her to Madame. On Thursdays there is a queue for the séances.
Al mercato, la vedova del mugnaio raccon.short: The widow tells everyone about the savings Madame found. There is a queue for the Thursday séances.

Al mercato, la vedova del mugnaio raccon.easy: At the market, the miller's widow tells anyone who will listen about the séance behind the bread stall. She found nothing, she says; but for the first time she slept. In the village they begin to say that the family from the estate comforts people better than the priest.
Al mercato, la vedova del mugnaio raccon.short: The widow says she found nothing, but slept. The village says you comfort people better than the priest.

Dalla bottega del bottaio, la notte, si.easy: At night, crying can be heard from the cooper's workshop. In the village they say the family from the estate has bought a dead child and keeps him in a glass case. It is not true; but it is not quite false either.
Dalla bottega del bottaio, la notte, si.short: At night crying comes from the cooper's. The village says you keep a dead child in a glass case.

La madre di Peti va a tutte le sedute de.easy: Peti's mother goes to every Thursday séance, in the front row, and now and then laughs to herself.
La madre di Peti va a tutte le sedute de.short: Peti's mother goes to every séance, and now and then laughs to herself.

Sul prato accanto al cimitero, quello ch.easy: On the field by the cemetery, the one the family sold, someone has driven in stakes with string, in neat rows, as if for a vegetable garden. Or for another cemetery.
Sul prato accanto al cimitero, quello ch.short: On the field you sold, someone has set stakes in rows, as for a garden. Or a cemetery.

La risposta la scrive chi in famiglia ha.easy: The reply is written by whoever in the family has the best handwriting, on estate paper, in a few polite and careful lines. The envelope, left under the door in the evening, is gone in the morning. In its place is a fresh black carnation, with a drop of dew that does not fall.
La risposta la scrive chi in famiglia ha.short: You reply in a few careful lines. In the morning, in place of the envelope, is a black carnation.

Le lettere bruciano bene, con una fiamma.easy: The letters burn well, with a high, cheerful flame, and for a few days no more come. Then one morning, in the cold fireplace, among the ashes, lies an envelope, whole, with black sealing wax and the open eye. It is not even scorched.
Le lettere bruciano bene, con una fiamma.short: You burn the letters. But one morning, among the ashes, lies an unburnt envelope.

Padre Anzelm ti aspetta sul sagrato con.easy: Father Anzelm is waiting for you on the church steps with his hat in his hand, and that alone is strange enough. He takes you to the old sacristy, behind the apse, which has not been used since they built the new one, and shows you a low little door of dark wood, shut with a rusty bolt.
Padre Anzelm ti aspetta sul sagrato con.short: Father Anzelm takes you to the old sacristy, to a little door shut with a bolt.

\"Da tre settimane\", dice, \"qualcuno b.easy: "For three weeks," he says, "someone has been knocking behind it. At night, at vespers, even during Mass. I opened it: it is an empty cupboard, the size of a confessional. I blessed it: they knock just the same." He rubs a hand over his face. "I want it bricked up. The mason wants three florins, and the parish has not got them. You, on the other hand, know all about knocking."
\"Da tre settimane\", dice, \"qualcuno b.short: "There has been knocking behind it for three weeks, even during Mass. I want it bricked up, but the parish has no money."

Il muratore lavora un pomeriggio intero,.easy: The mason works a whole afternoon, in silence, brick by brick, while the priest says the rosary in the doorway. When the last brick is in place, the knocking stops. Father Anzelm takes both your hands: it is the first time you have seen him smile.
Il muratore lavora un pomeriggio intero,.short: The door is bricked up, and the knocking stops. For the first time you see Father Anzelm smile.

Uscendo, guardi il muro fresco di calce..easy: As you leave, you look at the fresh mortar. You have the feeling, which you cannot explain, that one day someone will open it again and find behind it something that is not there now.
Uscendo, guardi il muro fresco di calce..short: You feel that one day someone will open that wall again, and find something that is not there now.

Il prete toglie il catenaccio di malavog.easy: The priest pulls back the bolt unwillingly. The cupboard is empty and dusty, smelling of old wax. But the inside of the door, at head height, is covered with knuckle marks: hundreds of little dents in the wood, some old and dark, others pale, as if from last night.
Il prete toglie il catenaccio di malavog.short: The cupboard is empty. But the inside of the door is covered in knuckle marks, some of them fresh.

In un angolo, sotto la polvere, c'è un r.easy: In a corner, under the dust, is a register bound in parchment: the exorcisms performed in that sacristy from 1711 to 1763, with names, dates and, in the margin, the number of knocks heard. The priest lets you take it away, as long as you never speak of it to him again. The next day the door is bricked up anyway.
In un angolo, sotto la polvere, c'è un r.short: There is also an eighteenth-century register of exorcisms, counting the knocks. The priest lets you take it.

Il Sindaco Bódi ti riceve nel suo uffici.easy: Mayor Bódi receives you in his office, a room with a portrait of the emperor, a smoking stove and a cupboard full of files no one has ever read. He is a fat, polite man with hands that are always damp, and he knows the price of everything: cows, votes, souls.
Il Sindaco Bódi ti riceve nel suo uffici.short: Mayor Bódi, fat and polite, knows the price of everything: cows, votes, souls.

\"Il consiglio dovrà decidere della sign.easy: "The council will have to decide about the lady of the caravan," he says, though you have not asked. "The priest has already been to see me. And so has a very elegant gentleman, with a flower in his buttonhole. They all ask me to speak. No one asks me what I need." He sighs. "The family from the estate, at least, are reasonable people."
\"Il consiglio dovrà decidere della sign.short: "The priest and a gentleman with a buttonhole flower want me to speak. No one asks what I need."

Il Sindaco conta le monete sulla scrivan.easy: The Mayor counts the coins on the desk as easily as counting sheep. He promises he will speak, and speak well. Then, walking you to the door, he tells you that the gentleman with the flower had offered him twice as much, "but with you, of course, it's different: you're local people".
Il Sindaco conta le monete sulla scrivan.short: The Mayor takes the money and promises to speak well. The gentleman with the flower, he admits, offered double.

Tiri fuori dal Journal una ricevuta ingi.easy: You take a yellowed receipt from the Journal: a loan your father made to old Bódi thirty years ago, which no one ever paid back. The Mayor goes pale, then red, then laughs, and the laugh does not reach his eyes.
Tiri fuori dal Journal una ricevuta ingi.short: You show him an old receipt: a loan never repaid. The Mayor laughs, but not with his eyes.

\"Parlerò come volete\", dice. \"Ma i Bó.easy: "I will speak as you like," he says. "But the Bódis have long memories. My son will have it, and my son's son." You leave with the receipt in your pocket and the feeling that you have made a very bad deal.
\"Parlerò come volete\", dice. \"Ma i Bó.short: "I will speak as you like. But the Bódis have long memories." It feels like a very bad deal.

Il Sindaco ascolta, annuisce, ti dà ragi.easy: The Mayor listens, nods, agrees with you on everything. He will speak against the medium, he says, because the village needs order and Masses, not little tables. He asks for nothing in return, and that makes you more suspicious than any demand.
Il Sindaco ascolta, annuisce, ti dà ragi.short: The Mayor will speak against the medium, and asks for nothing. That makes you suspicious.

Due giorni dopo vieni a sapere che la pa.easy: Two days later you learn that the parish has let him off the rent on a field for ten years. Father Anzelm, when you meet him, greets you like an ally.
Due giorni dopo vieni a sapere che la pa.short: Then you learn the parish has waived a rent for him. Father Anzelm greets you like an ally.

Tra le bancarelle del Farmer's Market c'.easy: Among the stalls of the Farmer's Market is a young man in a worn coat, with round glasses and a notebook open in his hand. His name is Béla Lukács, the village doctor's nephew: he studies medicine in Vienna and spends the summer in the village taking notes on everything, from the diseases of cows to the miracles of the lady of the caravan.
Tra le bancarelle del Farmer's Market c'.short: At the market is Béla Lukács, the doctor's nephew: he studies medicine in Vienna and takes notes on everything.

\"Non credo ai fantasmi\", ti dice, prim.easy: "I don't believe in ghosts," he says, before he has even introduced himself. "I believe in experiments. I have prepared a sealed envelope with a number inside: only I know it. If Madame Vámos reads it without opening it, I will be converted. But she won't let me into the caravan." He hands you the envelope. "You, on the other hand, she will."
\"Non credo ai fantasmi\", ti dice, prim.short: "I don't believe in ghosts. If Madame reads the number in this envelope without opening it, I'll be converted. You take it: she won't let me in."

Alla seduta posi la busta sul tavolino..easy: At the séance you put the envelope on the table. Madame barely touches it with her fingertips, closes her eyes and says: "Forty-seven." The next day young Lukács opens the envelope in front of you. It says forty-seven.
Alla seduta posi la busta sul tavolino..short: Madame touches the envelope and says: "Forty-seven." The envelope says exactly that.

Lui però non si converte. Prende la bust.easy: But he is not converted. He holds the envelope against the window light and scratches the seal with his nail. "Steam," he says, showing you a shadow along the edge of the wax. "Someone opened it and closed it again. I don't know when, or how. But I'll find out." He says goodbye with a small bow: he has found, he says, the first reasonable person in the village.
Lui però non si converte. Prende la bust.short: "Steam," says Lukács. "Someone opened it and closed it again. I'll find out." You are, he says, the first reasonable person in the village.

Gli ridi in faccia: in una famiglia di s.easy: You laugh in his face: in a family of scientists, a student with an envelope is an amateur. Young Lukács goes red to the ears, puts the envelope back in his pocket and leaves without a word.
Gli ridi in faccia: in una famiglia di s.short: You laugh in his face. Lukács goes red and leaves without a word.

Qualcuno, al mercato, ride con te. Lui s.easy: Someone at the market laughs with you. He turns round only once, at the corner, and looks at you the way one looks at a problem to be solved.
Qualcuno, al mercato, ride con te. Lui s.short: He turns round once, and looks at you like a problem to be solved.

Il carro di Madame Vámos non si muove da.easy: Madame Vámos's caravan has not moved in eight years: the wheels have sunk into the mud, grass grows on the roof and the velvet curtains have turned the colour of rust. Madame lets you in, gives you black tea in a chipped cup and studies you with her head on one side, the way one looks at a horse before buying it.
Il carro di Madame Vámos non si muove da.short: Madame's caravan has not moved in eight years. She gives you tea and studies you like a horse to buy.

\"Avete l'orecchio\", dice. \"Lo aveva a.easy: "You have the ear," she says. "Your father had it too, but he used it for talking. I can teach you to listen. I'm not asking for money." She smiles. "With your family, money comes later."
\"Avete l'orecchio\", dice. \"Lo aveva a.short: "You have the ear. I can teach you to listen. With your family, money comes later."

Le lezioni durano tutto l'inverno, il gi.easy: The lessons last all winter, on Thursday evenings. Madame teaches you to breathe slowly, to count the knocks, to leave your hands on the table without pushing. She also teaches you the tricks, the pedal, the thread, the throat voice, just as seriously as the rest. "Tricks are for the days when they don't answer," she says. "But one day they will answer you. Then you won't need me."
Le lezioni durano tutto l'inverno, il gi.short: All winter Madame teaches you to listen, and the tricks too. "One day they will answer you," she says.

Madame capisce subito il vero motivo del.easy: Madame understands at once why you really come, and is not offended. In fact she teaches you the tricks with a craftswoman's pride: the pedal, the silk thread, phosphorus dissolved in oil, the voice that comes out of the throat without moving the lips. You write them all down in a notebook.
Madame capisce subito il vero motivo del.short: Madame knows why you come, and teaches you the tricks with pride. You write them all down.

All'ultima lezione, chiudendo il quadern.easy: At the last lesson, as you close the notebook, she tells you just one thing: "Tricks are the easy part. The hard part is to stop using them when they are no longer needed."
All'ultima lezione, chiudendo il quadern.short: "Tricks are the easy part. The hard part is stopping when they are no longer needed."

Posi la tazza e ti alzi. Madame non ti t.easy: You put down your cup and stand up. Madame does not stop you. "As you like," she says, seeing you to the caravan door. "It doesn't matter. One of your children will come, or one of your grandchildren. Your blood always comes back." At the door she gives you a spiced biscuit, the way one does with children.
Posi la tazza e ti alzi. Madame non ti t.short: You refuse. "It doesn't matter," says Madame. "One of your children will come. Your blood always comes back."

Nel Park, vicino allo stagno, c'è una pa.easy: In the Park, near the pond, there is a cast-iron bench with a small brass plate: *Gift of the family of the estate, 1840*. Every evening at sunset an old woman sits there with a grey shawl and a basket on her knees, looking towards the hill. Someone tells you she was Father's nurse, in his last year.
Nel Park, vicino allo stagno, c'è una pa.short: Every evening, on the bench your family gave, sits Father's nurse, looking at the hill.

Quando ti siedi accanto a lei non si stu.easy: When you sit beside her she is not surprised. "You have his eyes," she says. "He didn't want to die in bed. He wanted to die sitting up, in the chair beside it, with his eyes open. He said that way he would see her coming."
Quando ti siedi accanto a lei non si stu.short: "You have his eyes. He wanted to die sitting up, eyes open, to see her coming."

La vecchia racconta senza fretta: la feb.easy: The old woman tells it slowly: the fever, the delirium, the formulas said aloud like prayers. At the end, she says, Father grew calm, looked at the door and said clearly: *"Here I am. Punctual as always."* Then he knocked once, with his knuckle, on the arm of the chair. "And someone answered," says the old woman, looking at the hill. "I was there."
La vecchia racconta senza fretta: la feb.short: At the end Father said: *"Here I am. Punctual as always."* He knocked once. "And someone answered," says the old woman. "I was there."

La vecchia prende il denaro, lo conta, l.easy: The old woman takes the money, counts it and puts it in her basket under a handkerchief. She thanks you as one thanks a relative. From that day, every week, a jar of blackberry jam appears on the estate doorstep, with a note in capitals: *"For the eyes."*
La vecchia prende il denaro, lo conta, l.short: Every week a jar of jam appears on your doorstep: *"For the eyes."*

Il fabbro svita la targhetta in un pomer.easy: The smith unscrews the plate in an afternoon. The bench stays, nameless, and the old woman still sits there every evening, but looks the other way, towards the village. A week later, where the plate was, someone has carved two initials with a knife: one is Father's. The other is an E.
Il fabbro svita la targhetta in un pomer.short: You remove the plate. A week later two initials are carved in its place: Father's, and an E.

A sorpresa prende la parola anche il nip.easy: To everyone's surprise the doctor's nephew speaks too, young Lukács, just back from Vienna with his degree: he tells of a sealed envelope opened and closed again with steam, and asks the council to inspect the caravan. The council thanks him and decides nothing.
A sorpresa prende la parola anche il nip.short: Young Lukács, just qualified, speaks too: he asks for the caravan to be inspected. The council decides nothing.

Il Sindaco Bódi, contro ogni abitudine,.easy: Mayor Bódi, quite unlike himself, speaks: of charity, of comfort for the bereaved, of the taxes Mrs Vámos pays on time. No one has ever heard him speak for so long.
Il Sindaco Bódi, contro ogni abitudine,.short: Mayor Bódi, quite unlike himself, speaks at length in favour of Mrs Vámos.

Il Sindaco Bódi parla poco e guarda spes.easy: Mayor Bódi says little and keeps looking at the family from the estate, like a dog looking at the master who has just beaten it.
Il Sindaco Bódi parla poco e guarda spes.short: Mayor Bódi says little, and looks at you like a beaten dog.

Il Sindaco Bódi, a sorpresa, si schiera.easy: Mayor Bódi, to everyone's surprise, takes the priest's side, and even quotes a verse from Leviticus, reading it from a scrap of paper.
Il Sindaco Bódi, a sorpresa, si schiera.short: Mayor Bódi, to everyone's surprise, takes the priest's side.

Il parroco, nel suo intervento, ringrazi.easy: The priest, in his speech, thanks "the generous families who paid for the work on the old sacristy". The wall, he says, is holding.
Il parroco, nel suo intervento, ringrazi.short: The priest thanks whoever paid for the sacristy wall. The wall, he says, is holding.

Si nota che uno degli eredi, il giovedì.easy: It is noticed that one of the heirs goes into Mrs Vámos's caravan on Thursday evenings and comes out late at night. No one says it aloud. Everyone writes it in the minutes with their eyes.
Si nota che uno degli eredi, il giovedì.short: Everyone knows that one of the heirs spends Thursday evenings in Madame's caravan. No one says so.

Madame Vámos vi riceve nel salotto nuovo.easy: Madame Vámos receives you in her new drawing room, still full of crates, with the piano playing by itself in the next room. She offers you plum brandy, thanks you one by one, and holds each hand a moment longer than she needs to. "We are neighbours now," she says. "For ever, if you like."
Madame Vámos vi riceve nel salotto nuovo.short: Madame thanks you one by one. "We are neighbours now," she says. "For ever, if you like."

Raggiungete il carro all'alba, sulla str.easy: You catch up with the caravan at dawn, on the main road, before the bridge. Madame Vámos has the horses stopped and listens to you from the driver's seat, without getting down. Then she slips off a silver ring and gives it to the youngest of you. "I'm not going far," she says. "No one ever goes far from here."
Raggiungete il carro all'alba, sulla str.short: At dawn Madame listens to you from the caravan and gives a ring to the youngest of you. "No one ever goes far from here."

Restate alla finestra della sala da pran.easy: You stay at the dining-room window, in the dark, watching. From the village come voices, some music, a barking dog; then nothing. None of you goes to bed before three. When at last you climb the stairs, the knocking on the walls goes with you, step by step, like a host showing the guests to their room.
Restate alla finestra della sala da pran.short: You stay at the window until three. When you go up to bed, the knocking follows you step by step.

Solo la camera del fondatore era rimasta.easy: Only the founder's bedroom had stayed as it was, as he had asked in writing: the bed with the shape of the body, the lamp, the chair by the bed. In seventeen years the chair had crept closer to the bed until it touched it.
Solo la camera del fondatore era rimasta.short: Only the founder's room had stayed as it was. In seventeen years the chair had crept up to touch the bed.

La camera del fondatore, svuotata tanti.easy: The founder's bedroom, cleared many years before, had become a laboratory like the others. Only the old chair, back from the kitchen who knows when, always stood in the same corner, facing the bed that was no longer there.
La camera del fondatore, svuotata tanti.short: The founder's room was a laboratory. But the old chair had come back, facing the bed that was gone.

La voce tace, ma non se ne va. La senti.easy: The voice stops, but does not go away. You can feel it waiting on the other side of the wall, patiently, like someone who has asked a question and knows the answer will come. The candle has burned down to the saucer. Outside it is starting to get light.
La voce tace, ma non se ne va. La senti.short: The voice stops, but waits for an answer. Outside it is getting light.

Bussi una volta, piano, con la nocca. Da.easy: You knock once, softly, with your knuckle. From the other side, after a very long silence, comes a single knock, light as a hand stroking your head. Then nothing. For the rest of the night you sleep deeply, without dreams, as you have not for years; and in the morning, on the wall near your pillow, is the mark of a knuckle that is not yours.
Bussi una volta, piano, con la nocca. Da.short: You knock once. A knock answers, light as a caress. You sleep as you have not slept in years.

Resti immobile sotto le coperte, con il.easy: You lie still under the covers, holding your breath. The voice waits a little longer, then moves away, room by room, like someone looking for another relative to talk to. At dawn the house is silent. You feel guilty, and lighter at the same time, like someone who has locked a door.
Resti immobile sotto le coperte, con il.short: You do not answer. The voice leaves, room by room. You feel guilty, and lighter.

Il Journal passa di mano in mano, sul ta.easy: The Journal goes from hand to hand on the breakfast table, among the crumbs. Each of you writes a few lines, and covers them with a hand until passing the notebook on. In the end there are more handwritings on the page than people at the table.
Il Journal passa di mano in mano, sul ta.short: Each of you writes in the Journal what you heard. In the end there are more handwritings than people at the table.

La proposta passa senza bisogno di votar.easy: The idea passes without a vote. From that day, at the estate, the dead are not mentioned at table, just as money and illness are not. But in the evening, in the corridors, everyone walks a little closer to the wall, as if to hear better.
La proposta passa senza bisogno di votar.short: No one speaks of the dead any more. But in the evening everyone walks close to the walls, to hear better.

La sede del Laborer's Union è una stanza.easy: The Laborer's Union meets in a smoky room above the smithy, with a long table, a rolled-up banner and a work register hanging on a nail. The smith now is Jóska: a man of thirty with broad shoulders, black hands and hair still singed at the front, as when he was a boy. He is the one who hands out work to the village masons.
La sede del Laborer's Union è una stanza.short: The smith is now Jóska, thirty years old, and he hands out work to the village masons.

Ti riconosce dalla faccia, o forse dal n.easy: He knows you by your face, or maybe your name. "Your parent gave me a coin once," he says, "and asked me to teach them a game. I never forgot it."
Ti riconosce dalla faccia, o forse dal n.short: "Your parent gave me a coin once. I never forgot it."

Ti riconosce dal nome, e il sorriso gli.easy: He knows you by your name, and stops smiling. "Your mother, or your father, I don't remember which, had me slapped in front of the forge. I was six. Some things you don't forget."
Ti riconosce dal nome, e il sorriso gli.short: "Your parent had me slapped. I was six. You don't forget that."

Nel registro, tra un tetto da rifare e u.easy: In the register, between a roof to be mended and a chimney to be swept, there are many identical lines, all with the same heading: *Circle of the Last Hour – work on the walls*. Private houses, nearly all of them widows'. Jóska sees where you are looking, and shuts the register.
Nel registro, tra un tetto da rifare e u.short: The register lists many jobs of *work on the walls* for the Circle, in widows' houses. Jóska shuts it.

Jóska prende il denaro, lo conta e ne ch.easy: Jóska takes the money, counts it and asks for the same again. Then, quietly, he explains everything with a craftsman's contempt for an easy job.
Jóska prende il denaro, lo conta e ne ch.short: Jóska wants double. Then he explains it all, with contempt.

Jóska rifiuta il denaro. Poi, a bassa vo.easy: Jóska will not take the money. Then, quietly, he explains everything, as a way of returning a favour.
Jóska rifiuta il denaro. Poi, a bassa vo.short: Jóska refuses the money, and explains everything, as if repaying a favour.

Un'intercapedine nel muro, larga un palm.easy: A gap in the wall, a hand's width, beside the widow's bed; a padded little hammer hanging from a rope; the rope running down to the cellar, where a boy paid two kreuzer a night waits for the signal. "One knock for yes, two for no," says Jóska, and for a moment he looks like the boy behind the forge again. "But I never worked at the estate. Your walls knock by themselves. They did it when I was little."
Un'intercapedine nel muro, larga un palm.short: A gap in the wall, a hammer, a boy in the cellar. "But I never worked at the estate," says Jóska. "Your walls knock by themselves."

Jóska gira per la tenuta un giorno inter.easy: Jóska goes round the estate for a whole day, knocking on the walls with his knuckles and his hammer handle, listening the way a doctor listens to a sick chest. The walls are solid, he says: brick and mortar, no gaps, no ropes.
Jóska gira per la tenuta un giorno inter.short: Jóska checks every wall in the estate. They are solid: no gaps, no ropes.

Solo nella parete della camera grande, q.easy: Only in the wall of the big bedroom, the one that was your grandfather's, does the hammer sound hollow. Jóska makes a hole, and inside is a coil of copper wire, green with age, carefully wound round an iron core. Someone bricked it in there, many years ago. On the core, scratched with the point of a nail, is a number: 1848.
Solo nella parete della camera grande, q.short: Only in your grandfather's room does the wall sound hollow. Inside is a coil of copper wire on an iron core, scratched 1848.

Padre Anzelm ascolta, annuisce, e la dom.easy: Father Anzelm listens, nods, and the next Sunday gives half his sermon to the smith. The Circle stops giving him work; the widows stop greeting him; the masons look for another leader.
Padre Anzelm ascolta, annuisce, e la dom.short: Father Anzelm preaches against the smith. Jóska loses his work and the village's respect.

Jóska non dice niente a nessuno. Ma quan.easy: Jóska says nothing to anyone. But when you pass the smithy, the hammer on the anvil beats a rhythm you know, slow and stubborn: one, two, one.
Jóska non dice niente a nessuno. Ma quan.short: Jóska says nothing. But when you pass, his hammer beats: one, two, one.

Il becchino Mihály è ancora lì, più gran.easy: Mihály the gravedigger is still there, bigger and more bent, with a white beard and the same cap. He takes you to your grandfather's grave, the one with the brass tube, without being asked.
Il becchino Mihály è ancora lì, più gran.short: Old Mihály takes you to your grandfather's grave, the one with the brass tube.

Il tubo è aperto, e intorno al tumulo l'.easy: The tube is open, and the grass around the grave is trampled. "They come at night," the gravedigger explains, "from all over the village. They talk into the tube. They say the old man carries messages to the other dead, like a post office." He shows you a tin box full of folded notes. "Some push them inside. I take them out in the morning. I don't read them."
Il tubo è aperto, e intorno al tumulo l'.short: People come at night to talk into the tube: they say the old man carries messages to the other dead.

Il piombo che chiudeva il tubo è ancora.easy: The lead that sealed the tube is still there. But it is no longer level with the brass: it sticks out a finger's width, swollen and cracked, as if something had pushed it from below, patiently, for twenty-five years.
Il piombo che chiudeva il tubo è ancora.short: The lead in the tube sticks out a finger's width, cracked, as if pushed from below for twenty-five years.

Il coperchio del tubo non c'è più: lo ce.easy: The tube's cap is gone: they searched for it for a long time after the fortieth day and never found it. The bell, though, is still there, and on nights without wind, says the gravedigger, it rings.
Il coperchio del tubo non c'è più: lo ce.short: The cap is gone. The bell, says the gravedigger, rings on windless nights.

Il tubo è chiuso, come lo chiuse il becc.easy: The tube is closed, as the gravedigger closed it after the forty days. The brass has turned green. Mihály says that in twenty-five years no one from the family has ever stopped to look at it.
Il tubo è chiuso, come lo chiuse il becc.short: The tube is closed and green. In twenty-five years no one from the family has come to look at it.

Dal tubo sale lo stesso freddo, lo stess.easy: The same cold rises from the tube, the same smell of wax. And this time a sound that is not a knock: the steady scratch of a pen on paper, far below, like someone writing without stopping. Now and then the pen stops, and you hear someone blowing on the ink.
Dal tubo sale lo stesso freddo, lo stess.short: From the tube comes the sound of a pen writing, far below, without stopping.
