Mihály riempie il tubo di terra, poi di.easy: Mihály fills the tube with earth, then mortar, then pours over it the holy water Father Anzelm gave him for the purpose. Last of all he takes off the bell and buries it beside the headstone.
Mihály riempie il tubo di terra, poi di.short: Mihály fills the tube with earth and mortar, and buries the bell.

La sera, al cimitero, è tutto silenzioso.easy: In the evening the cemetery is silent. At the estate, though, for a whole week the knocking on the walls is faster and louder, like someone locked out.
La sera, al cimitero, è tutto silenzioso.short: The cemetery is silent. At the estate, for a week, the knocking sounds like someone locked out.

Il Sindaco Bódi, figlio del vecchio Bódi.easy: Mayor Bódi, old Bódi's son, is a man of forty with a waxed moustache and a gold watch he keeps checking. In the town hall courtyard are the coils of copper wire for the imperial telegraph line, which will reach {0} within the year; and the Mayor, they say, is the only one who knows how many there really are.
Il Sindaco Bódi, figlio del vecchio Bódi.short: The new Mayor Bódi keeps the copper coils for the telegraph. Only he knows how many there really are.

\"Mio padre diceva che la vostra famigli.easy: "My father said your family pays well and asks no questions," he says, stroking his moustache. "That is a rare quality."
\"Mio padre diceva che la vostra famigli.short: "My father said you pay well and ask no questions."

\"Mio padre mi ha parlato di voi\", dice.easy: "My father told me about you," he says, without smiling. "And about a certain receipt. I hope your memory is shorter than his."
\"Mio padre mi ha parlato di voi\", dice.short: "My father told me about you, and about a certain receipt."

\"Mio padre diceva che la vostra famigli.easy: "My father said your family sides with the priest," he says, raising an eyebrow. "I wonder what the priest wants with a telegraph."
\"Mio padre diceva che la vostra famigli.short: "My father said you side with the priest. What does the priest want with a telegraph?"

Ti mostra le bobine come un mercante mos.easy: He shows you the coils the way a merchant shows silk. One, he says, could easily get lost. Coils do get lost, in storerooms.
Ti mostra le bobine come un mercante mos.short: One coil, he says, could easily get lost.

Il Sindaco intasca il denaro senza conta.easy: The Mayor pockets the money without counting it. The coil arrives at the estate at night, on a council cart, driven by an usher in livery who raises his hat at the gate.
Il Sindaco intasca il denaro senza conta.short: The coil arrives at night, on a council cart.

Entri nel cortile del municipio dopo mez.easy: You get into the town hall courtyard after midnight, with a sack and a dark lantern. The coil weighs as much as a man. As you drag it out, a first-floor window lights up: behind the glass is the Mayor in his nightshirt, who watches you, raises his candle in greeting and goes back to bed.
Entri nel cortile del municipio dopo mez.short: You steal the coil at night. The Mayor sees you from his window, raises his candle and goes back to bed.

Il giorno dopo, nel registro del magazzi.easy: The next day, in the storeroom register, the coil is listed as "delivered to the estate, paid".
Il giorno dopo, nel registro del magazzi.short: The register lists it as "delivered to the estate, paid".

Gli dici che la tua famiglia non compra.easy: You tell him your family does not buy council property under the counter. The Mayor laughs, checks his watch and shows you out very politely. The next day the Gazette prints a short piece praising "the honesty of the notable families our town hall has the honour to serve".
Gli dici che la tua famiglia non compra.short: You refuse. The next day the Gazette praises "the honesty of the notable families".

Il comune ha deciso di prosciugare lo st.easy: The council has decided to drain the park pond: too many mosquitoes, too many bad smells, too many accidents. The workmen open the sluice one Monday morning, and for three days the water slowly drops, uncovering the black bottom, which stinks of leaves and iron. Half the village comes to watch, handkerchiefs over their noses.
Il comune ha deciso di prosciugare lo st.short: The council drains the park pond. Half the village comes to look at the black bottom.

Sul fondo, nel fango, ci sono centinaia.easy: On the bottom, in the mud, are hundreds of things: coins, rings, locks of hair tied with ribbon, photographs, letters sealed in bottles. For thirty years the mothers and widows of {0} have secretly thrown them into the pond, for their dead. In the middle, at the deepest point, is a child's ice skate, its strap still buckled.
Sul fondo, nel fango, ci sono centinaia.short: In the mud lie thirty years of gifts for the dead: rings, letters, locks of hair. In the middle is a child's skate.

Qualcuno, tra la folla, dice il nome di.easy: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name. His old mother, in the front row, looks at the skate without crying.
Qualcuno, tra la folla, dice il nome di.short: Someone says Peti's name. His old mother looks at the skate without crying.

Qualcuno, tra la folla, dice il nome di.easy: Someone in the crowd says Peti's name, then looks at you. In the village some stories are never forgotten.
Qualcuno, tra la folla, dice il nome di.short: Someone says Peti's name, and looks at you. Some stories are never forgotten.

Le lettere sono indirizzate ai morti, e.easy: The letters are addressed to the dead, and the dead have not opened them. You open them, one by one, in the evening, in the laboratory. Wives telling husbands about the harvest, mothers asking their children if they are cold, an old man apologising to someone for a quarrel in 1831. In the last bottle is a single sheet in a child's hand: *"I'm not cold."* The bottle was sealed with wax, and the wax is new.
Le lettere sono indirizzate ai morti, e.short: You read the letters to the dead. In the last bottle, sealed recently, a child has written: *"I'm not cold."*

Il parroco benedice il fondo dello stagn.easy: The priest blesses the bottom of the pond with his bucket and sprinkler, under the hostile eyes of the widows, then has the letters, photographs and hair piled on the bank and sets fire to them. The smoke is sweet and heavy. The skate does not burn: they bury it in a corner of the cemetery, without a name. The widows do not forgive you. Their daughters, perhaps, will thank you one day.
Il parroco benedice il fondo dello stagn.short: The priest burns everything. The skate will not burn: they bury it. The widows do not forgive you.

Ti chini nel fango con un sacco, insieme.easy: You crouch in the mud with a sack, alongside the village boys and a few shameless grown-ups. The coins come from thirty years of different mintings, some silver. The widows watch you from the bank, in silence. That night, at the estate, the knocking on the walls is wet: it leaves little rings of water on the plaster.
Ti chini nel fango con un sacco, insieme.short: You gather the coins while the widows watch. That night the knocking leaves rings of water on the walls.

Al Builder's Office c'è agitazione: scav.easy: There is a stir at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the Circle's Temple, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
Al Builder's Office c'è agitazione: scav.short: Digging for the Circle's Temple, the workmen find a lead box.

Al Builder's Office c'è agitazione: scav.easy: There is a stir at the Builder's Office: digging the foundations of the new post office, the workmen have found a lead box, buried two metres down, under a squared stone.
Al Builder's Office c'è agitazione: scav.short: Digging for the new post office, the workmen find a lead box.

Il capomastro la tiene sul tavolo come u.easy: The foreman keeps it on the table as if it were a bomb. On the lid, scratched with a nail, are a date and three letters: *1828 – C. U. O.* No one dares open it. Someone thought of calling the family from the estate, who "know about these things".
Il capomastro la tiene sul tavolo come u.short: On the lid is scratched *1828 – C. U. O.* No one dares open it, so they call you.

Dentro, su un fondo di velluto marcito,.easy: Inside, on a bed of rotten velvet, are three locks of hair tied with black ribbon: one brown, one black, one fair. Beside them, a silver bell with no clapper. And a folded sheet, with three signatures and one sentence: *"Whoever leaves first, knock."* One of the signatures is the one you see every evening on the first page of the Journal.
Dentro, su un fondo di velluto marcito,.short: Inside are three locks of hair and a sheet with three signatures: *"Whoever leaves first, knock."* One is the Journal's.

Porti la cassetta, chiusa, alla sede del.easy: You take the box, unopened, to the Circle's house. A tall gentleman with a black carnation receives you, and takes it in his hands as one holds a newborn baby. "We thought we had lost it," he says. "Thank you. Your grandfather would be pleased." He walks you to the door, and there puts an envelope in your hand. Inside are some money and a lock of brown hair, tied with black ribbon.
Porti la cassetta, chiusa, alla sede del.short: The gentleman with the black carnation thanks you: "Your grandfather would be pleased." He gives you an envelope with money and a lock of hair.

Il parroco benedice la cassetta senza ap.easy: The priest blesses the box without opening it, with a grimace, and the workmen bury it again in a corner of the cemetery, under a stone. That night, at the estate, the knocks come in threes, always three, in three different places in the house, like three people looking for each other and never meeting.
Il parroco benedice la cassetta senza ap.short: The box is buried. That night there is knocking in three places in the house, like three people looking for each other.

Il fabbro Jóska, quando gli mostro le ta.easy: When I show Jóska the smith the drawings, he studies them without touching them, his hands behind his back. Then he says he has seen the soft-iron core in the drawing before: it is the one he found bricked into the wall of the big bedroom, with the number 1848 scratched on it.
Il fabbro Jóska, quando gli mostro le ta.short: Jóska recognises in the drawing the iron core he found in the wall, the one marked 1848.

Il rame, almeno, non manca: la bobina de.easy: At least there is no shortage of copper: the imperial telegraph coil is in the cellar, wrapped in a cloth, and no one at the town hall has ever looked for it.
Il rame, almeno, non manca: la bobina de.short: There is copper: the telegraph coil is in the cellar.

Alcuni lettori collegano la nebbia al pr.easy: Some readers link the fog to the draining of the park pond. Where there was water, they say, there is now a hole; and in {0} holes always fill up with something else.
Alcuni lettori collegano la nebbia al pr.short: Some link the fog to the drained pond: in {0} holes always fill up with something else.

Il vecchio becchino Mihály, infine, assi.easy: Finally, old Mihály the gravedigger swears that every evening the fog starts from the same spot: the grave of the first master of the estate, the one with the brass tube.
Il vecchio becchino Mihály, infine, assi.short: The gravedigger says the fog starts every evening from the grave with the brass tube.

Uscite in giardino con le lanterne, tutt.easy: You go out into the garden with lanterns, all together, holding hands like children. Three steps from the door the house disappears. Ten steps further you disappear too, from each other, and only your voices remain, calling each other's names. Too many voices answer. You come back after an hour, count yourselves at the door, and the number is right. Fortunately.
Uscite in giardino con le lanterne, tutt.short: You go out into the fog. You call each other's names, and too many answer. Back inside you count yourselves: luckily, you are all there.

Chiudete le imposte, mettete le spranghe.easy: You close the shutters, bar the doors, stuff the cracks with wet rags. The fog stays outside, against the glass, white and patient like an animal waiting to come in. Around midnight someone knocks at the front door, three times, politely. No one goes to open it. In the morning there are wet footprints on the doorstep, coming but not going.
Chiudete le imposte, mettete le spranghe.short: You bar everything. At midnight someone knocks three times at the door. In the morning there are footprints coming but not going.

Nella nebbia il cimitero non ha più conf.easy: In the fog the cemetery has no edges: the headstones come out of the white one by one, like teeth, and the low wall cannot be seen. Somewhere among the graves children are playing hide-and-seek. You hear the counting, the laughter, feet running on the gravel. There are five of them. Then, when they call each other by name, there are six.
Nella nebbia il cimitero non ha più conf.short: In the foggy cemetery children play hide-and-seek. There are five. When they call their names, there are six.

Il sesto ha otto anni, i vestiti bagnati.easy: The sixth is eight years old, with wet clothes and pink cheeks. None of the others knows his name; they say he only comes to play when there is fog, and that he is the best of all at hiding.
Il sesto ha otto anni, i vestiti bagnati.short: The sixth is eight, with wet clothes. He only comes with the fog, and he is the best at hiding.

Lo vedi sparire dietro una lapide piccol.easy: You see him vanish behind a small headstone with a stone angel: the one your family paid for, many years ago, for the cooper's son.
Lo vedi sparire dietro una lapide piccol.short: You see him vanish behind the angel headstone your family paid for, for the cooper's son.

Lo vedi frugare tra le tombe, una per un.easy: You see him searching the graves one by one, reading the names with his finger. A child asks what he is looking for. "Mine," he answers. "I can't find it."
Lo vedi frugare tra le tombe, una per un.short: You see him searching the graves. "Mine," he says. "I can't find it."

Ti torna in mente, chissà perché, una fr.easy: Something comes back to you, who knows why, a story told in your family: a medium, a vigil, a child who "will play with the others again, when the fog comes".
Ti torna in mente, chissà perché, una fr.short: You remember a family story: a child who "will play with the others again, when the fog comes".

Conti fino a cinquanta con la fronte con.easy: You count to fifty with your forehead against a headstone, as when you were small. You find them all, one after another, except him. You look for him until the fog turns grey, then blue, then black. In the end he finds you: a small hand, cold as January water, touches your shoulder. "Found you," he says, and laughs. When you turn round there is no one there, and your clothes are wet up to the elbow.
Conti fino a cinquanta con la fronte con.short: You play, and cannot find him. In the end a cold hand touches your shoulder: "Found you." You turn: no one. You are wet to the elbow.

Raduni i bambini e li riporti in paese,.easy: You gather the children and take them back to the village, one at a time, to their mothers. The mothers thank you, then look at their children, then at the fog behind you, and shut the door faster than they need to. You brought back five children. No one asks about the sixth.
Raduni i bambini e li riporti in paese,.short: You take the children home: five of them. No one asks about the sixth.

Il bambino si avvicina senza paura e ti.easy: The child comes up to you without fear and tells you his name: Peti. Then he asks you about his mother. She is old now, and lives alone behind the cooper's workshop; you tell him, and he nods, as if he already knew. "Tell her I'm not cold any more," he says. "You tell her: she can't hear me."
Il bambino si avvicina senza paura e ti.short: "I'm Peti. Tell my mother I'm not cold any more. You tell her: she can't hear me."

Vai dalla vecchia quella sera stessa. No.easy: You go to the old woman that same evening. She does not ask how you know. She sits you down, pours you a drink and listens to it all without crying. When you leave, the fog has lifted.
Vai dalla vecchia quella sera stessa. No.short: You tell his mother. She listens without crying. When you leave, the fog has lifted.

Accanto al banco della chiromante c'è un.easy: Next to the fortune teller's stall is a new black tent, with a hand-painted sign: **HARTMANN – SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPHY – VIENNA, PARIS, LONDON**. Mr Hartmann is a small, kind man, with fingers stained by silver nitrate. In front of the tent hang his portraits: widows, soldiers, children in stiff poses; and behind them, blurred and see-through, their dead, with a hand on the shoulder of the living.
Accanto al banco della chiromante c'è un.short: Mr Hartmann does **SPIRIT PHOTOGRAPHY**: in his portraits, behind the living, stand their dead.

\"Con questa nebbia\", dice, \"le lastre.easy: "With this fog," he says, "the plates come out as never before. The veil is thin here: my camera feels it." He looks at you with the eye of someone working out a pose. "And you have quite a few dead in the family."
\"Con questa nebbia\", dice, \"le lastre.short: "With the fog the plates come out wonderfully. And you have plenty of dead in the family."

Resti immobile per un minuto intero, con.easy: You stay still for a whole minute, your neck held in an iron clamp, while the photographer counts aloud. The portrait is ready two days later. There you are, stiff-backed and pale; and behind you, only a little lighter than the fog, is your parent, with a hand on your shoulder.
Resti immobile per un minuto intero, con.short: In your portrait, behind you, stands your parent, with a hand on your shoulder.

Riconosci la mano prima del volto: le di.easy: You know the hand before the face: the ink-stained fingers, the ring that went into the coffin. When you point it out, Mr Hartmann turns very serious and will not take your money.
Riconosci la mano prima del volto: le di.short: You recognise the ring that went into the coffin. Hartmann will not take your money.

Rovesci il tavolo delle lastre, e il vet.easy: You overturn the table of plates, and the glass shatters on the gravel with a sound like little bells. The photographer does not react: he looks at you with endless pity, like a customer who has not understood.
Rovesci il tavolo delle lastre, e il vet.short: You smash the plates. The photographer looks at you with pity, like a customer who has not understood.

Raccogliendo i cocci per non lasciarli a.easy: Gathering the pieces so the children won't find them, you find one bigger than the rest, with part of a portrait still whole: a shoulder, a hand, and a face you know from family photographs. The plate is from three days ago. No one in your family has ever sat for a portrait here.
Raccogliendo i cocci per non lasciarli a.short: Among the shards is a face you know from family photos. The plate is from three days ago.

Il signor Hartmann ride, conta le monete.easy: Mr Hartmann laughs, counts the coins and lets you into the tent. The trick is simple: the plate is exposed twice, once with the customer and once with the portrait of the dead person, which the family gives him without realising, by answering his kind questions. A gauze veil over the lens does the rest.
Il signor Hartmann ride, conta le monete.short: The trick is simple: the plate is exposed twice, once with the customer and once with a portrait of the dead.

Poi, mentre ti accompagna fuori, si ferm.easy: Then, as he walks you out, he stops in front of a plate hung up to dry. "This one, though, no," he says quietly. "I didn't make this one." He will not let you look at it.
Poi, mentre ti accompagna fuori, si ferm.short: Then he points to a hanging plate: "I didn't make this one." He won't let you see it.

Dopo la messa, mentre esci dalla chiesa,.easy: After Mass, as you leave the church, a twelve-year-old boy runs after you with his surplice still on, ears sticking out and the look of someone who has thought hard before deciding. His name is Benedek, and he is Father Anzelm's altar boy: the one who yawns at every Mass for the dead.
Dopo la messa, mentre esci dalla chiesa,.short: After Mass Benedek, Father Anzelm's twelve-year-old altar boy, runs after you.

Ti trascina dietro un pilastro e ti racc.easy: He pulls you behind a pillar and tells you, all in one breath, that the sexton secretly copies the register of the dead every evening, and on Thursdays takes the copies to a gentleman with a black flower in his buttonhole. And more: the sexton listens to confessions from the sacristy, through the grille. "The Circle knows everything about everyone," he says. "That's why the dead know so much at the séances." He is scared, and it shows.
Ti trascina dietro un pilastro e ti racc.short: The sexton, he says, copies the register of the dead and listens to confessions for the Circle. "That's why the dead know so much at séances."

Padre Anzelm caccia il sagrestano il gio.easy: Father Anzelm dismisses the sexton that very day, without a word, with a wave of the hand worth more than an excommunication. In his place he takes the boy, who from then on serves Mass with his ears red with pride.
Padre Anzelm caccia il sagrestano il gio.short: Father Anzelm dismisses the sexton and takes the proud boy in his place.

Benedek non dimentica chi lo ha ascoltat.easy: Benedek does not forget who listened to him. Every time he meets you he takes off his cap; and now and then he quietly tells you what he hears in the sacristy.
Benedek non dimentica chi lo ha ascoltat.short: Benedek does not forget: he always greets you, and tells you what he hears.

Il sagrestano accetta il tuo denaro con.easy: The sexton takes your money as easily as he takes the Circle's. From that day you know before anyone who has died, who is dying and who has confessed what; and you reach grieving families with a word of comfort before the gravedigger does.
Il sagrestano accetta il tuo denaro con.short: The sexton takes your money too. Now you reach grieving families before the gravedigger.

Benedek ti guarda passare dalla porta de.easy: Benedek sees you go by the sacristy door on Thursdays, with a face you will not forget. He has understood everything. He is twelve, and has just learned how the world works.
Benedek ti guarda passare dalla porta de.short: Benedek sees you go by on Thursdays. He is twelve, and has just learned how the world works.

Gli dici che le faccende della sacrestia.easy: You tell him that sacristy business is none of yours, and that an altar boy who tells tales comes to a bad end. The boy goes red, lowers his head and goes back into the church without a word.
Gli dici che le faccende della sacrestia.short: You tell him to mind his own business. He goes back into the church without a word.

La domenica dopo, alla messa, non sbadig.easy: The next Sunday, at Mass, he no longer yawns. He watches you all through the service, from the altar, with the eyes of a grown man.
La domenica dopo, alla messa, non sbadig.short: The next Sunday he no longer yawns. He watches you from the altar with a grown man's eyes.

Il Sindaco Bódi ha convocato il consigli.easy: Mayor Bódi has called a special meeting of the council. In the fog, he says, people go out at night to look for their dead, and do not always come back: three missing since September, one found at dawn in the cemetery, sitting on a grave that was not his family's, talking to himself. He proposes a curfew: no one in the streets from dusk to dawn, until the fog lifts.
Il Sindaco Bódi ha convocato il consigli.short: In the fog people go out to look for their dead, and do not always come back. The Mayor proposes a curfew.

Le famiglie del Circolo protestano: i mo.easy: The Circle's families protest: the dead, they say, only speak at night. The priest approves. The Mayor looks at the family from the estate, the way one watches the needle of a scale.
Le famiglie del Circolo protestano: i mo.short: The Circle protests, the priest approves. The Mayor looks at you: it is your call.

Il coprifuoco passa con un voto di scart.easy: The curfew passes by one vote. From that evening the watchmen go round with lanterns and a hand bell, and anyone found in the street spends the night at the town hall. At night the streets of {0} are empty; but the watchmen say that the bell sometimes rings on its own, and that someone in the fog answers.
Il coprifuoco passa con un voto di scart.short: The curfew passes. The streets are empty at night, but the watchmen's bell sometimes rings on its own.

Il coprifuoco non passa. La sera stessa.easy: The curfew does not pass. That very evening the streets fill with lanterns: widows, mothers, old people walking to the cemetery in procession, singing softly. Some stop to thank you. A woman takes your hand and tells you that tonight, at last, she will be able to talk to her son.
Il coprifuoco non passa. La sera stessa.short: The curfew fails. The streets fill with lanterns, and a mother thanks you: tonight she will talk to her son.

Al Builder's Office ti aspetta il capoma.easy: At the Builder's Office the foreman Szabó is waiting for you, an honest and frightened man. A year ago he built a house for a young married couple, at the end of the mill road: new bricks, new beams, nothing old. Since the fog came, the walls knock. The couple are sleeping at the mother-in-law's.
Al Builder's Office ti aspetta il capoma.short: The foreman Szabó built a new house. Since the fog came, its walls knock.

Il fabbro Jóska giura di non averci mai.easy: Jóska the smith swears he never touched it, and Szabó believes him: he built every wall himself, and knows there is nothing inside them. "You," he says, "are the only ones who can tell me whether I built a house or a door."
Il fabbro Jóska giura di non averci mai.short: Jóska had nothing to do with it. "You tell me whether I built a house or a door," says Szabó.

Passi la notte su una sedia, al centro d.easy: You spend the night on a chair in the middle of the empty bedroom, with a candle and the Journal. At midnight the knocking starts, in the north wall, the one facing the estate. You count the knocks. You write them down. At dawn you have three pages of letters that make no words, but that, read backwards, spell the name of the street where you were born.
Passi la notte su una sedia, al centro d.short: You spend the night there writing down the knocks. Read backwards, they spell the street where you were born.

Gli operai abbattono il muro in una matt.easy: The workmen knock down the wall in one morning. There is nothing inside: bricks, mortar, a mouse's nest. The knocking stops. The couple go home, and the foreman thanks you with tears in his eyes. Only Jóska the smith, looking at the rubble, pulls a face: among the bricks is a child's shoe, small and wet, that no one put there.
Gli operai abbattono il muro in una matt.short: The wall comes down, and the knocking stops. But among the bricks is a child's wet shoe.

Fai una seduta a regola d'arte, come que.easy: You hold a perfect séance, just like Madame's: candles, joined hands, a throat voice, a pedal hidden under the rug. You announce that the spirit has gone in peace. The couple cry with gratitude and pay you well. For a week the knocking really stops. Then it starts again, louder; and one knock, they tell you, sounds like a laugh.
Fai una seduta a regola d'arte, come que.short: You hold a fake séance and are paid well. The knocking stops for a week, then returns louder, like laughter.

Lasci una moneta sul velluto. La medium.easy: You leave a coin on the velvet. The medium does not look at it; she holds your hand and whispers a name, that of a village family who have just lost someone and who, she says, need you more than you need the dead. You go the next day. She is right.
Lasci una moneta sul velluto. La medium.short: The medium whispers the name of a grieving family who need you. You go. She is right.

Mentre la medium accompagna fuori un'alt.easy: While the medium shows another client out, you bend down under the table. The pedal is there, just as in the stories of those who visited the caravan long ago. But it is covered in dust, and the dust has not been touched for months.
Mentre la medium accompagna fuori un'alt.short: Under the table is the pedal. But it is dusty, and no one has used it for months.

Mentre nessuno ti guarda, ti chini sotto.easy: While no one is looking, you bend down under the table. No pedals, no threads, no holes in the floor: only old wood and a child's shoe, small and wet, that no one knows anything about.
Mentre nessuno ti guarda, ti chini sotto.short: Under the table there are no tricks: only a child's wet shoe.

Il fotografo Hartmann, invitato dalla fa.easy: Hartmann the photographer, invited by the family, has set up his camera in a corner, the plate ready and the magnesium in its dish.
Il fotografo Hartmann, invitato dalla fa.short: In a corner Hartmann the photographer stands ready.

Il fotografo Hartmann, nonostante le las.easy: Hartmann the photographer, despite the broken plates, has come with a new camera, and no one has dared send him away.
Il fotografo Hartmann, nonostante le las.short: Hartmann the photographer has come anyway, with a new camera.

Per una notte, coprifuoco o no, le strad.easy: For one night, curfew or no curfew, the village streets are full of lanterns: anyone who wants to crosses the fog to come and see.
Per una notte, coprifuoco o no, le strad.short: For one night the streets are full of lanterns: everyone wants to see.

Sulla porta, con la cotta sotto il cappo.easy: At the door, his surplice under his coat and a bucket of holy water in his hand, stands Benedek the altar boy, sent by Father Anzelm "to watch and to remember".
Sulla porta, con la cotta sotto il cappo.short: At the door stands Benedek, sent by Father Anzelm "to watch and to remember".

Al Builder's Office il capomastro srotol.easy: At the Builder's Office the foreman unrolls the plan of the new road on the table, the one that will link the square to the telegraph station. It runs right over the Kovács family's old mill, idle for almost thirty years, with its rotten wheel and caved-in roof. Next week they are knocking it down.
Al Builder's Office il capomastro srotol.short: The new road runs over the old Kovács mill. Next week they knock it down.

Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.easy: The name rings a bell. Your family used to tell of a widow, a séance made up behind the bread stall, and a brick behind the stove with nothing behind it.
Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.short: Your family told of a widow and a brick behind the stove, with nothing behind it.

Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.easy: The name rings a bell. Your family used to tell of a widow, of Madame Vámos, of the seventh paddle of the wheel. Later the widow left the mill to the Circle; and now the Circle is selling it for the road.
Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.short: Your family told of the seventh paddle. Later the widow left the mill to the Circle, which is now selling it.

Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.easy: The name rings a bell. Your family used to tell of an honest widow and a hen; and of a miller who trusted no one, not even dead.
Il nome ti dice qualcosa. In famiglia si.short: Your family told of a miller who trusted no one, not even dead.

Tu, del resto, sai già che cosa c'era di.easy: You already know, of course, what was behind the mill stove: a private séance at the Pub led you to it. But a miller who trusted no one, you think, would not have put everything in one place.
Tu, del resto, sai già che cosa c'era di.short: You already found the box behind the stove. But a miller like that, you think, would not keep everything in one place.

\"Se volete dare un'occhiata prima che a.easy: "If you want to have a look before the pickaxes come," says the foreman, "go ahead. There's nothing left inside. Everyone says so."
\"Se volete dare un'occhiata prima che a.short: "Have a look if you like. There's nothing left inside."

La stufa è una massa di mattoni anneriti.easy: The stove is a heap of blackened bricks, covered in swallows' nests. The third brick from the bottom moves under your fingers. Behind it is a rusty tin box, and inside a roll of old coins and a note written in charcoal: *"For my wife. Someone tell her, because I can't."*
La stufa è una massa di mattoni anneriti.short: Behind the third brick is a box of coins and a note: *"For my wife. Someone tell her, because I can't."*

Era dietro la stufa. Lo era sempre stato.easy: It was behind the stove. It always had been. A fake séance, twenty-five years ago, had told the truth; and no one had looked carefully enough.
Era dietro la stufa. Lo era sempre stato.short: It was behind the stove. A fake séance, twenty-five years ago, had told the truth.

Il che vuol dire, pensi, che i soldi che.easy: Which means, you think, that the money Madame found for her under the seventh paddle was something else. Who had put it there? And why?
Il che vuol dire, pensi, che i soldi che.short: So the money under the seventh paddle was something else. Who put it there?

Mandi a chiamare i nipoti della vedova K.easy: You send for the widow Kovács's grandsons, two young carters, and tell them to search the mill before the pickaxes come. They come back in the evening with a tin box found behind the stove, and tears in their eyes. Inside were their grandfather's savings, and a note for their grandmother.
Mandi a chiamare i nipoti della vedova K.short: The widow's grandsons find their grandfather's savings behind the stove, and a note for their grandmother.

La vedova è morta da anni. I ragazzi por.easy: The widow has been dead for years. The young men take the note to the cemetery and bury it beside her with their own hands. Then they come to the estate to thank you, caps in hand.
La vedova è morta da anni. I ragazzi por.short: The widow is dead. The young men bury the note beside her, and come to thank you.

Padre Anzelm sta morendo, e lo sa. Non l.easy: Father Anzelm is dying, and he knows it. He tells no one: every morning he goes to the cemetery with his stick and walks among the graves like someone looking over a house to buy. The day he meets you he stops at your grandfather's grave, the first of your family, and points with his stick at the patch of grass beside it.
Padre Anzelm sta morendo, e lo sa. Non l.short: Father Anzelm is dying. At the cemetery he stops at your grandfather's grave and points to the spot beside it.

\"Questo posto è vostro\", dice. \"La vo.easy: "This plot is yours," he says. "Your family bought it along with the other one, in 1848. I'd like it." He coughs, for a long time. "To keep an eye on him. Thirty years of sermons, and I never managed to make him be quiet. Perhaps from close by."
\"Questo posto è vostro\", dice. \"La vo.short: "I'd like to be buried here, beside him. To keep an eye on him. Perhaps from close by I can make him be quiet."

Poi aggiunge, quasi tra sé: \"Il muro de.easy: Then he adds, almost to himself: "The sacristy wall is holding. But since you paid for it, I sometimes wonder who I had it bricked up for."
Poi aggiunge, quasi tra sé: \"Il muro de.short: "The sacristy wall is holding. But sometimes I wonder who I had it bricked up for."

Poi aggiunge, quasi tra sé: \"Il registr.easy: Then he adds, almost to himself: "The register someone in your family took from the sacristy. I hope someone in your house has read it. I never had the courage."
Poi aggiunge, quasi tra sé: \"Il registr.short: "I hope someone has read the register your family took from the sacristy. I never had the courage."

Il vecchio prete ti stringe la mano con.easy: The old priest shakes your hand with his dry, warm fingers. He dies in November, and they bury him where he asked, a step from your grandfather, his head pointing the same way. The whole village comes to the funeral, even the Circle's widows, at the back, veils lowered.
Il vecchio prete ti stringe la mano con.short: Father Anzelm dies in November and is buried beside your grandfather. The whole village comes to the funeral.

La notte dopo il funerale, alla tenuta,.easy: The night after the funeral, at the estate, no one knocks. Nor the night after, nor the one after that. Then, on the fourth night, the knocking starts again: but now there are two rhythms, one over the other, like two old men arguing.
La notte dopo il funerale, alla tenuta,.short: For three nights no one knocks. Then the knocking returns, in two rhythms, like two old men arguing.

Padre Anzelm annuisce senza offendersi,.easy: Father Anzelm nods without taking offence, as if he had expected it. "You're right," he says. "Each to his own." They bury him in November on the other side of the cemetery, by the wall, his headstone turned towards your grandfather's grave.
Padre Anzelm annuisce senza offendersi,.short: "You're right. Each to his own." They bury him across the cemetery, his headstone turned towards your grandfather.

Il Circolo, saputo del tuo rifiuto, ti m.easy: The Circle, hearing of your refusal, sends you a black-edged card with one word: *Thank you.* You are not sure what for.
Il Circolo, saputo del tuo rifiuto, ti m.short: The Circle sends you a card: *Thank you.* You are not sure what for.

Il prete ti guarda a lungo, appoggiato a.easy: The priest looks at you for a long time, leaning on his stick. Then he sits down on your grandfather's headstone, without respect, as one sits on a bench. "Your name," he says. "They knocked it out letter by letter. In the sacristy walls, in the alms box, in the wood of the confessional. I did thirty years of exorcisms, and every time they stopped they began again from the start, like a schoolboy going over his lessons."
Il prete ti guarda a lungo, appoggiato a.short: "Your name," he says. "For thirty years they knocked it out letter by letter, in the church walls."

Si alza, a fatica. \"Il posto tenetevelo.easy: He gets up with difficulty. "Keep the plot," he adds. "I've changed my mind. I don't want to be near the one who listens." They bury him in November, on the other side of the cemetery.
Si alza, a fatica. \"Il posto tenetevelo.short: "Keep the plot. I don't want to be near the one who listens." They bury him far away.

Il medico condotto di {0}, adesso, è Bél.easy: The village doctor of {0} is now Béla Lukács: a man of fifty with a grey beard, round glasses and a leather bag he never lets go of. He took over from his uncle, along with a certain name for blasphemy, because he says in public that the dead do not come back and that anyone who swears they see them has a bad liver.
Il medico condotto di {0}, adesso, è Bél.short: The doctor is now Béla Lukács. He says in public that anyone who sees the dead has a bad liver.

\"La vostra famiglia mi aiutò, una volta.easy: "Your family helped me once," he says, "with a sealed envelope. It was the first reasonable person I met in this village. I hope common sense runs in families."
\"La vostra famiglia mi aiutò, una volta.short: "Your family helped me once. I hope common sense runs in families."

\"La vostra famiglia mi rise in faccia,.easy: "Your family laughed in my face once," he says, "at the market, in front of everyone. I was twenty-seven. Let's see if you laugh too."
\"La vostra famiglia mi rise in faccia,.short: "Your family laughed in my face once. Let's see if you laugh too."

Sul tavolo della sala del consiglio c'è.easy: On the council table there is a petition: the doctor asks the Mayor for permission to inspect the places where séances are held "for reasons of hygiene", and to seize anything suspicious he finds: phosphorus, gauze, threads, bells. The signatures of the important families are missing.
Sul tavolo della sala del consiglio c'è.short: The doctor wants to inspect the séance rooms. The important families have not signed.

La tua è la prima firma, e la più grande.easy: Yours is the first signature, and the biggest. The inspection takes place on a rainy Tuesday, with two gendarmes and the doctor in the lead: phosphorus in a cupboard, rolls of gauze, a bell with a wire disappearing into the ceiling. The Circle says these are for cleaning. The village laughs for a week, and then forgets.
La tua è la prima firma, e la più grande.short: You sign first. The inspection finds phosphorus, gauze and wires. The village laughs for a week, then forgets.

Lukács no. Ti ringrazia, ti prescrive gr.easy: Lukács does not. He thanks you, prescribes you a sleeping draught that works, free of charge, and from that day greets you in the street like a colleague.
Lukács no. Ti ringrazia, ti prescrive gr.short: Lukács does not: he gives you a sleeping draught that works, and greets you like a colleague.

Il medico si toglie gli occhiali, li pul.easy: The doctor takes off his glasses, cleans them with his handkerchief and puts them back on very calmly. "I see," he says. "It runs in the family." The petition stays on the table without your signatures, and the Mayor puts it in a drawer.
Il medico si toglie gli occhiali, li pul.short: "I see," says the doctor. "It runs in the family." The petition ends up in a drawer.

Due giorni dopo, sulla soglia della tenu.easy: Two days later, on the estate doorstep, you find a black carnation and an envelope of money, with no note. The Circle knows how to show its gratitude.
Due giorni dopo, sulla soglia della tenu.short: On the doorstep you find a black carnation and some money. The Circle knows how to be grateful.

Alla sede del Laborer's Union c'è una ri.easy: At the Laborer's Union there is an unusual meeting: six gravediggers from the district, caps in hand, with the faces of men who have not slept for weeks. Old Mihály, the village gravedigger, speaks for all of them. They will no longer bury anyone after sunset, and they will no longer nail coffins shut, because for some time now, when they lower a coffin into the grave, someone knocks from inside.
Alla sede del Laborer's Union c'è una ri.short: The gravediggers will not bury after sunset any more: when they lower a coffin, someone knocks.

\"Non i morti di adesso\", precisa Mihál.easy: "Not the new dead," Mihály explains. "The old ones, in the graves next door. They knock to greet the newcomers." Until the estate does something about it, he adds, the district's cemeteries will stay closed in the evening.
\"Non i morti di adesso\", precisa Mihál.short: "The old dead knock, to greet the new." Until the estate does something, the cemeteries stay closed at night.

I becchini accettano il denaro e tornano.easy: The gravediggers take the money and go back to work, but only by day, and only three to a grave: one digs, one holds the lantern, one prays. Mihály thanks you with a nod. Burials in {0} become very quick indeed.
I becchini accettano il denaro e tornano.short: Paid, the gravediggers go back to work, but only by day and three to a grave: one digs, one holds the light, one prays.

Scavi tu, di notte, con la pala del nonn.easy: You dig yourself, at night, with your grandfather's spade and a dark lantern. The earth is soft and cold. When the coffin reaches the bottom, from the grave next door comes one knock, then another, polite, like someone knocking at a new neighbour's door. You answer with the spade handle. Afterwards, for some reason, you feel like a guest in someone else's house.
Scavi tu, di notte, con la pala del nonn.short: You dig at night. From the next grave comes polite knocking, as if greeting a new neighbour. You answer with the spade.

Mihály, la mattina dopo, ti offre un fav.easy: The next morning Mihály offers you a favour of the trade, as his father did for your family.
Mihály, la mattina dopo, ti offre un fav.short: Mihály offers you a favour of the trade, as his father did for your family.

Il parroco benedice le pale, le funi e l.easy: The priest blesses the spades, ropes and lanterns of every gravedigger in the district, in a short and slightly silly ceremony in the presbytery yard. It works, or so it seems: all winter, in the cemeteries, no one knocks. The gravediggers go back to work, and the priest, for the first time in years, invites you to lunch.
Il parroco benedice le pale, le funi e l.short: The priest blesses the spades. All winter no one knocks, and the priest invites you to lunch.

La chiromante del villaggio è una donna.easy: The village fortune teller is a fat, cheerful woman, with rings on every finger and a scruffy parrot on a perch. For two coins she reads anyone's palm, and usually says nice things. When she takes yours, though, she stops smiling.
La chiromante del villaggio è una donna.short: The fortune teller reads everyone's palm and always says nice things. But when she takes yours, she stops smiling.

\"Avete due linee della vita\", dice, se.easy: "You have two lifelines," she says, tracing them with her nail. "One is yours. The other begins before you were born, and doesn't end. I've never seen it on anyone. Well: I saw it once, on a gentleman from the estate, long ago, when I was a girl."
\"Avete due linee della vita\", dice, se.short: "You have two lifelines. One is yours. The other starts before you and never ends. I've only seen it on a gentleman from the estate, long ago."

La chiromante esita, poi parla piano, pe.easy: The fortune teller hesitates, then speaks quietly, so the parrot won't hear. "It means someone lives in you too," she says. "Someone who hasn't finished. You are his hand, when he wants to write." She folds your fingers into a fist, gently, the way one folds a letter. She will not take money.
La chiromante esita, poi parla piano, pe.short: "Someone lives in you too. Someone who hasn't finished. You are his hand, when he wants to write."

La chiromante intasca le monete e giura.easy: The fortune teller pockets the coins and swears on the parrot that she will tell no one. The parrot, which heard it all, repeats at the market that same evening, in the fortune teller's voice, *"two lines, two lines"*, until someone throws a cloth over it.
La chiromante intasca le monete e giura.short: The fortune teller swears to keep quiet. But the parrot repeats at the market: *"two lines, two lines"*.

Le prendi la mano e le dici, con voce gr.easy: You take her hand and tell her gravely that she has a son far away, a bad back and a secret about money. She laughs till she cries: you have guessed it all, because everyone her age has a son far away, a bad back and a secret about money. "You have a gift," she says. "But I didn't make up the two lines on your hand."
Le prendi la mano e le dici, con voce gr.short: You read her palm with the usual tricks, and she laughs. "You have a gift. But I didn't make up the two lines on your hand."

Si ricorda che il defunto Padre Anzelm,.easy: It will be remembered that the late Father Anzelm, in his last year, often condemned this sort of business. Until a new parish priest is appointed, the parish is in the care of the vicar from the next village, who has not yet said anything.
Si ricorda che il defunto Padre Anzelm,.short: Father Anzelm condemned such business. The vicar standing in for him has said nothing yet.

Il medico condotto, dottor Lukács, ha fa.easy: The village doctor, Dr Lukács, has let it be known that he will support no candidate "who sits at little tables". His letter was received with great interest and no consequences.
Il medico condotto, dottor Lukács, ha fa.short: Dr Lukács will support no one "who sits at little tables". No one takes any notice.

Si segnala infine che i cimiteri del dis.easy: Finally, the district's cemeteries have returned to normal service after the winter strike. Burials after sunset remain suspended "until further notice".
Si segnala infine che i cimiteri del dis.short: The cemeteries have reopened. But no one is buried after sunset any more.

Il Circolo, però, non era morto: si riun.easy: The Circle, however, was not dead: it still met, behind closed doors and with the best lawyers in the province, in its black marble Temple behind the town hall.
Il Circolo, però, non era morto: si riun.short: But the Circle was not dead: it still met in secret, in its Temple behind the town hall.

Il Tempio del Circolo, una costruzione b.easy: The Circle's Temple, a low black marble building behind the town hall, had been built in the eighties, long after the woman of the caravan had left. No one knew whose money paid for it. Everyone had an idea.
Il Tempio del Circolo, una costruzione b.short: The Circle's Temple had been built in the eighties. No one knew whose money paid for it, but everyone had an idea.

La chiesa è piena a metà. Padre Benedek.easy: The church is half full. Father Benedek says Mass quickly, his ears red with cold, and afterwards comes to shake your hands on the steps, one by one, as with new parishioners. In the square, from the Circle's windows, someone is watching you.
La chiesa è piena a metà. Padre Benedek.short: Father Benedek shakes your hands like new parishioners. From the Circle's windows someone watches you.

Il salone del Circolo ha le poltrone di.easy: The Circle's hall has velvet armchairs, electric lamps with violet shades and a portrait from 1828 above the fireplace. They seat you in the front row, without asking who you are. During the séance the table knocks out your family's name, and two hundred people turn to look at you, smiling, as one smiles at a relative who is late for lunch.
Il salone del Circolo ha le poltrone di.short: At the séance the table knocks out your family's name. Two hundred people turn to smile at you.

Restate alla tenuta, tra i bauli e la po.easy: You stay at the estate, among the trunks and the dust, opening windows no one had opened in years. In the pockets of the coats hanging in the hall you find notes, pebbles, a dried carnation, a milk tooth. None of you throws anything away.
Restate alla tenuta, tra i bauli e la po.short: You stay home. In the pockets of the old coats you find notes, pebbles, a dried carnation, a milk tooth.

Le due voci tacciono insieme, come a un.easy: The two voices fall silent together, as if at a signal. In the silence you hear your heart, the tick of the clock in the corridor and, very far away, the hum of the electric wires. You have time for one question only: you know it without being told.
Le due voci tacciono insieme, come a un.short: The voices fall silent. You may ask one question only.

Le voci esitano. Poi rispondono insieme,.easy: The voices hesitate. Then they answer together, with one sentence, which they repeat until you write it down: *"That you finish what he began."* They do not say what. In the morning, in the Journal, the page where you wrote it is folded in four, carefully, like a letter to be sent.
Le voci esitano. Poi rispondono insieme,.short: *"That you finish what he began."* They do not say what.

Le voci ridono, piano, e non è una risat.easy: The voices laugh, softly, and it is not an unkind laugh. "Live," says the older one. "Live, and don't listen too much." The other adds something about windows, which should be opened in the morning, and bread, which should be eaten warm. Then the knocking moves away, and the night ends the way ordinary nights do.
Le voci ridono, piano, e non è una risat.short: "Live," say the voices. "And don't listen too much." The night ends like an ordinary night.

Poi ti guarda meglio, e sorride sotto la.easy: Then he looks at you more closely, and smiles under his beard. "Your family has helped me before, once or twice," he says. "I remember reasonable people well. There have not been many."
Poi ti guarda meglio, e sorride sotto la.short: "Your family has helped me before. I remember reasonable people."

Poi ti guarda meglio, e il sorriso gli s.easy: Then he looks at you more closely, and his smile cools. "Your family has never taken me seriously," he says. "I haven't come for an apology. I've come to give you a chance."
Poi ti guarda meglio, e il sorriso gli s.short: "Your family never took me seriously. But I'm giving you a chance."

Il dottore ti stringe la mano con una fo.easy: The doctor shakes your hand with surprising strength for his age, and leaves you a card with the address of his office at the University. "Come whenever you like," he says. "In daylight, if possible."
Il dottore ti stringe la mano con una fo.short: The doctor gives you his card. "Come whenever you like. In daylight, if possible."

Lukács non si offende. Si rimette il cap.easy: Lukács is not offended. He puts his hat back on, wishes you good day and goes slowly down the steps. At the bottom he turns. "The Circle," he says, "has never needed your loyalty. It needs your blood. Think about it."
Lukács non si offende. Si rimette il cap.short: "The Circle doesn't need your loyalty," says Lukács. "It needs your blood. Think about it."

Il dottore annuisce, come chi è abituato.easy: The doctor nods, like someone used to waiting. "It has taken me fifty years," he says. "I can wait a little longer." He leaves his card on the hall table, under the vase of flowers.
Il dottore annuisce, come chi è abituato.short: "I've waited fifty years. I can wait a little longer." He leaves you his card.

L'edificio sorge sul prato accanto al ci.easy: The building stands on the field by the cemetery, the one with the nettles and the gravedigger's goats, which your family sold half a century ago to a society of discreet people. From the bell tower without a bell, dozens of thin wires run taut to the graves.
L'edificio sorge sul prato accanto al ci.short: The building stands on the field your family sold. Wires run from its bell tower to the graves.

L'edificio lo riconosci prima ancora di.easy: You recognise the building before you go in: it is the one in the drawing your family copied from memory fifty years ago, with the bell tower but no bell and the wires stretched to the graves, like harp strings.
L'edificio lo riconosci prima ancora di.short: You recognise the building: it is the one in the drawing your family copied fifty years ago.

L'edificio sorge dall'altra parte del ci.easy: The building stands on the other side of the cemetery, on the land the Circle bought when your family would not sell its own. From the bell tower without a bell, dozens of thin wires run taut to the graves.
L'edificio sorge dall'altra parte del ci.short: The building stands on the land the Circle bought when you would not sell yours. Wires run from its bell tower to the graves.

Padre Benedek è un uomo alto e ossuto, c.easy: Father Benedek is a tall, bony man, with the sticking-out ears he had as an altar boy and a cassock worn at the elbows. Since he became parish priest he has kept a register: the names of everyone who goes to the Circle, the dates of the séances, the offerings, the suspicious deaths. The register has grown to three crates, and the three crates no longer fit in the presbytery.
Padre Benedek è un uomo alto e ossuto, c.short: Father Benedek keeps a register of everything the Circle does. It now fills three crates, too many for the presbytery.

Ti accoglie come un vecchio alleato. \"L.easy: He greets you like an old ally. "Your family listened to me when I was twelve and no one believed me," he says. "Now it's my turn to listen to you."
Ti accoglie come un vecchio alleato. \"L.short: "Your family listened to me when I was twelve. Now it's my turn."

Ti accoglie con una cortesia fredda e pr.easy: He greets you with cold, exact politeness. "I remember your family," he says. "I was twelve. I learned a great deal that day."
Ti accoglie con una cortesia fredda e pr.short: "I remember you," he says coldly. "I was twelve. I learned a lot that day."

Ti porta nella sacrestia vecchia, davant.easy: He takes you to the old sacristy, to a brick wall roughly plastered and hidden behind a walnut wardrobe. "Behind here is a cupboard bricked up in Father Anzelm's day. No one has looked at it for fifty years, and no one will for another fifty. I want to put the crates in there. I need someone to pay the mason, and to tell no one."
Ti porta nella sacrestia vecchia, davant.short: Behind a walnut wardrobe is the cupboard Father Anzelm bricked up. Benedek wants to hide the crates there, and needs someone to pay the mason.

Tu sai, dai racconti di famiglia, che co.easy: You know, from family stories, what is on the inside of that door: hundreds of knuckle marks.
Tu sai, dai racconti di famiglia, che co.short: You know there are hundreds of knuckle marks inside that door.

Il muratore apre il muro in un'ora. Il r.easy: The mason opens the wall in an hour. The cupboard is empty and dry; on the inside of the little door are the knuckle marks, darkened with age, and no one mentions them. You put in the priest's three crates and, beside them, three more: the diaries, minutes and letters of your family, fifty years of papers no one at home had the courage to read again.
Il muratore apre il muro in un'ora. Il r.short: In the cupboard you place the priest's three crates and three crates of your family's papers.

Il muratore richiude in fretta, male, co.easy: The mason bricks it up again in a hurry, badly, with the leftover bricks. Father Benedek blesses the wall, then puts the wardrobe back in front of it. "Someone will find them one day," he says. "Let's hope it's a patient person."
Il muratore richiude in fretta, male, co.short: The wall is bricked up again, badly. "Someone will find them one day," says Benedek. "Let's hope they're patient."

Il muratore apre il muro, ci sistemate l.easy: The mason opens the wall, you put in the priest's crates, the mason closes it again. You watch it all from the doorway with your hands in your pockets. That evening your family's papers are still in the study at the estate, in the trunk at the foot of the desk. It seems wiser. It also seems to you, as you close the trunk, that you hear knocking from inside.
Il muratore apre il muro, ci sistemate l.short: You pay, but the family papers stay in the trunk at home. As you close it, you seem to hear knocking from inside.

Dici al parroco che le faccende della pa.easy: You tell the priest that parish business is none of yours. Father Benedek does not insist. He finds another mason and someone else to pay, and the sacristy wall is not mentioned again. The Circle, however, does mention it: that same evening a black carnation is tucked into the handle of the estate door.
Dici al parroco che le faccende della pa.short: You want nothing to do with it. Benedek finds someone else. But that evening there is a black carnation on your door.

La National Bank occupa il palazzo con l.easy: The National Bank is in the building with the fake marble columns, the one that replaced the old one-room Bank. The manager is a young man with a perfect parting and a leather-bound ledger that looks older than he is. It is the ledger of the bank's oldest account: your family founder's, opened in 1828 and never closed.
La National Bank occupa il palazzo con l.short: The manager of the National Bank shows you its oldest account: your founder's, opened in 1828.

Da settant'anni, il primo di ogni mese,.easy: For seventy years, on the first of every month, a deposit has come from Vienna, later from Budapest, signed with three initials: C. U. O.
Da settant'anni, il primo di ogni mese,.short: For seventy years a monthly deposit signed C. U. O. has arrived.

E da cinquant'anni, il secondo giorno di.easy: And for fifty years, on the second day of every month, someone from your family has come to collect it. "Admirably regular," says the manager, without irony. "Like a pension."
E da cinquant'anni, il secondo giorno di.short: And for fifty years your family has collected it. "Like a pension," says the manager.

Dopo che la tua famiglia lo rifiutò, il.easy: After your family refused it, the sender stopped asking for it to be sent back. The money has piled up in a separate account, with interest, for half a century. The manager shows you the balance with a certain reverence.
Dopo che la tua famiglia lo rifiutò, il.short: The money your family refused has piled up for half a century. The manager shows it to you with reverence.

Accanto a ogni versamento c'è lo stesso.easy: Beside each deposit is the same black carnation drawn in ink, and the same name, *O. Garai*, with the same pressure of the pen, from 1828 to this morning. The president of the Circle of the Last Hour, the manager tells you quietly, has that name.
Accanto a ogni versamento c'è lo stesso.short: Every deposit, from 1828 to today, is signed *O. Garai*. That is the name of the Circle's president.

Il direttore conta il denaro in una stan.easy: The manager counts the money in a separate room, with two clerks and a steel door. You leave with a full leather bag and the feeling, which you cannot shake, that someone has just paid you for something. For what, you will learn at the end.
Il direttore conta il denaro in una stan.short: You leave with a bag full of money, and the feeling that someone has paid you for something.

Firmi la chiusura del conto. Il direttor.easy: You sign to close the account. The manager hesitates, then rules a line under the last figure and writes *closed* in his best hand. The pen spits a drop of ink onto the page, right on top of the word.
Firmi la chiusura del conto. Il direttor.short: You close the account. The manager writes *closed*, and the pen spits a drop of ink onto the word.

Il primo del mese successivo, alla Natio.easy: On the first of the next month, a deposit arrives at the National Bank from Budapest for an account that no longer exists. The bank sends it back. Another comes the next day. Then another.
Il primo del mese successivo, alla Natio.short: The next month a deposit arrives for the closed account. Then another, and another.

Il direttore, lusingato di essere preso.easy: The manager, pleased to be taken seriously, shows you where the money goes: a Budapest company, the same one that bought the new shops on the square; then the Circle's funeral parlour; then a smith, a pharmacist, a photographer, a retired sexton. Fifty years of wages. These are not a spiritualist society's expenses: they are a theatre's.
Il direttore, lusingato di essere preso.short: The Circle's money pays a smith, a pharmacist, a photographer, a sexton. It is not a spiritualist society: it is a theatre.

Copi tutto su un taccuino. Uscendo, ti a.easy: You copy it all into a notebook. As you leave, you notice that a page of the ledger, the one for 1848, has been torn out. The manager swears it was there yesterday.
Copi tutto su un taccuino. Uscendo, ti a.short: You copy it all. But the page for 1848 has been torn out. The manager swears it was there yesterday.

Alla Public Library, nella sala dei fond.easy: At the Public Library, in the rare books room, the librarian hands you, wearing gloves, a small book bound in card: *Des tables parlantes et des esprits frappeurs*, Paris, 1827. It comes, she says, from the library of your family's founder, sold at auction to pay debts in 1857. It is the booklet someone saw on Father's shelf on the first night.
Alla Public Library, nella sala dei fond.short: The library has the French booklet on talking tables, the one on the founder's shelf on the first night.

I margini sono fitti di appunti, in due.easy: The margins are full of notes, in two hands. One is the Journal's. The other is small, elegant, a woman's. The two hands answer each other, correct each other, tease each other. At the bottom of the last page, under the date 1828, are three names one under another, as in a contract: the founder's, *Eszter Vámos* and *O. Garai*. And above them, underlined: *Circle of the Last Hour*.
I margini sono fitti di appunti, in due.short: On the last page, under the date 1828, are three names: the founder, *Eszter Vámos* and *O. Garai*. And above them: *Circle of the Last Hour*.

Aspetti che la bibliotecaria si volti, e.easy: You wait for the librarian to turn away, and the page tears off with a sound that seems deafening to you. At home you burn it in the stove. The paper curls and blackens, and for a moment, before it turns to ash, the three names glow red, one under another.
Aspetti che la bibliotecaria si volti, e.short: You tear out the page and burn it. Before turning to ash, the three names glow red.

Il fondatore della tua famiglia, dunque,.easy: So your family's founder was not just a correspondent of the Circle. He founded it. And the knocking on the first night, perhaps, surprised no one but his children.
Il fondatore della tua famiglia, dunque,.short: The founder did not just write to the Circle: he founded it. Perhaps the first night's knocking surprised only his children.

Il dottor Lukács legge i margini due vol.easy: Dr Lukács reads the margins twice, with a magnifying glass, then takes off his glasses and rubs his eyes. "Three friends," he says, "a doctor, an actress and a businessman, who in 1828 invent a society for talking to the dead. It's the proof I've been looking for for forty years." Then he puts his glasses back on. "Or the proof that someone, in 1828, already knew what would happen."
Il dottor Lukács legge i margini due vol.short: "Three friends who in 1828 invent a society for talking to the dead," says Lukács. "It's the proof I wanted. Or proof that they already knew what would happen."

Rimetti il libretto nella sua scatola e.easy: You put the booklet back in its box and return it to the librarian with a smile. You tell no one: not the family, not Dr Lukács, not the Circle. But at night, at the estate, you find yourself knocking softly on your bedroom wall, once, as if asking permission; and from the other side someone answers, with a patience that sounds satisfied.
Rimetti il libretto nella sua scatola e.short: You tell no one. But at night you find yourself knocking softly on the wall; and someone answers, satisfied.

Nella sede del Laborer's Union, un elett.easy: At the Laborer's Union a thin young electrician comes up to you like someone selling stolen goods. He worked on the wiring of the Circle's Temple, he says, and during a séance he hid a phonograph behind a curtain, for a bet with his mates. The wax cylinder is in a hatbox, wrapped in cotton wool.
Nella sede del Laborer's Union, un elett.short: An electrician secretly recorded a Circle séance, on a wax cylinder.

\"Ci sono le voci\", sussurra. \"Quelle.easy: "The voices are on it," he whispers. "The dead ones. I didn't want to hear it again. Nor did the others." He wants to be rid of it, and wants the family from the estate to have it: you, he says, will know what to do with it.
\"Ci sono le voci\", sussurra. \"Quelle.short: "The voices of the dead are on it. You take it: you'll know what to do with it."

La puntina gratta, fruscia, e poi si sen.easy: The needle scratches and hisses, and then you hear voices in a room, coughs, a creaking table. Then one voice closer than the rest, hoarse, as if recorded through a brass tube. It says your family's name, and then yours, clearly, twice. On the cylinder's label is a date: two years before you came to town.
La puntina gratta, fruscia, e poi si sen.short: A hoarse voice says your name, twice. But the cylinder dates from two years before you came to town.

Il dottor Lukács ascolta il cilindro tre.easy: Dr Lukács listens to the cylinder three times, the last time slowing the phonograph with his finger. At the right speed, the "dead man's" voice is Mr Garai's, with a carnation in his mouth, one might say, and a brass tube at his lips. The doctor writes it all down and thanks you. Then he adds, more quietly, that there is another voice, at the end of the recording, which he cannot place, and which he did not want to slow down.
Il dottor Lukács ascolta il cilindro tre.short: Slowed down, the "dead man's" voice is Garai's. But at the end is another voice, which Lukács cannot place.

Il cilindro si spezza in tre pezzi sul s.easy: The cylinder breaks into three on the cobbles, like a biscuit. The electrician looks hugely relieved, thanks you twice and leaves almost at a run. That evening, at the café on the square, the phonograph plays by itself, for a minute, a song no one put on.
Il cilindro si spezza in tre pezzi sul s.short: You break the cylinder. That evening the café phonograph plays a song by itself.

È l'anno del censimento, e al Town Hall.easy: It is census year, and at the Town Hall the clerk for the hill district, a young man with glasses and inky fingers, stops you in the corridor with the estate's form in his hand. He has a problem, he says, and does not know how to write it down.
È l'anno del censimento, e al Town Hall.short: It is census year. The clerk stops you with the estate's form: he has a problem.

La sera della sua visita, quando è passa.easy: On the evening of his visit, when he came to count the residents, he saw the family at table in the dining room, through the window. He counted one person per chair, as one does. There were eleven chairs. On the form, however, the family listed only the living; and he would like to know who the others were, to be thorough.
La sera della sua visita, quando è passa.short: Through the window he counted eleven people at table. The form lists only the living. Who were the others?

Firmi. Il modulo va a Budapest con gli a.easy: You sign. The form goes to Budapest with the others, and the estate appears in the Kingdom's statistics as the most crowded house in the province. A few months later a letter comes from the central office, asking for the ages of "seven residents not on the register". No one answers. The letter, on the hall table, turns yellow overnight.
Firmi. Il modulo va a Budapest con gli a.short: You sign "eleven". Budapest asks for the ages of "seven unregistered residents". No one answers.

L'impiegato corregge il numero con un so.easy: The clerk corrects the number with a sigh of relief. He thanks you: he thought he was going mad. As you leave the town hall you look towards the hill, and for a moment you seem to see, at the dining-room windows, figures moving away, offended, like guests told that dinner is over.
L'impiegato corregge il numero con un so.short: You have the number corrected. At your windows you seem to see figures leaving, offended.

L'impiegato descrive con precisione da c.easy: The clerk describes them with a bookkeeper's precision: an old gentleman at the head of the table, with a notebook; a lady with a black shawl; two people who look very like your parents; an old couple holding hands; and a child in wet clothes, playing with the crumbs. "They were all eating," he says. "That's what struck me. No one touched their plate, but they were all eating."
L'impiegato descrive con precisione da c.short: An old man with a notebook, a lady in a black shawl, your parents, a wet child. "No one touched their plate, but they were all eating."

Negli ambienti della Public Library si p.easy: At the Public Library there is talk of a French booklet from 1827, once owned by an important family, whose last pages are said to be of interest for the history of the Circle. The librarian declines to comment.
Negli ambienti della Public Library si p.short: At the library there is talk of a French booklet with interesting pages about the Circle.

Alla National Bank, intanto, il conto pi.easy: At the National Bank, meanwhile, the oldest account in town has shown unusual activity in the last month. The manager reminds readers that bank secrecy is sacred, like the secrecy of confession.
Alla National Bank, intanto, il conto pi.short: The National Bank's oldest account has shown odd activity. The manager will not talk.

Circola infine la voce di una registrazi.easy: Finally, there is a rumour of a phonograph recording made in secret at one of the Circle's séances. Those who say they have heard it swear that one of the voices speaks the name of a living person.
Circola infine la voce di una registrazi.short: There is talk of a secret recording of the Circle, in which a voice speaks a living person's name.

Il negozio vende guanti. La commessa è g.easy: The shop sells gloves. The shop assistant is very kind, pale, and in no hurry. While you try on a pair of grey gloves, three knocks come from the back room, one, two, one; the assistant smiles and says it is the cat. You leave with the new gloves. They are cold, and stay cold all winter.
Il negozio vende guanti. La commessa è g.short: You buy gloves. Three knocks come from the back: "It's the cat." The gloves stay cold all winter.

La lettera esce il martedì, in terza pag.easy: The letter comes out on Tuesday, on page three, signed with the family's full name. Dr Lukács cuts it out and pins it up in his office. The Circle does not reply. But on Wednesday, outside every new shop, there is a vase of fresh black carnations, one in each window.
La lettera esce il martedì, in terza pag.short: The letter appears in the Gazette. The Circle does not reply, but black carnations appear outside every new shop.

Nella corsia comune dello Hospital, tra.easy: In the Hospital's common ward, between a man with consumption and a man with both legs in plaster, lies an old man whose lungs have been burned by fifty years at the forge. He breathes with a whistle, and every breath is an effort. It is Jóska, the smith. He asked the nuns to send for someone from the estate, and the nuns, shocked, did as he asked.
Nella corsia comune dello Hospital, tra.short: In hospital lies Jóska, the old smith, his lungs burned by the forge. He has asked to see someone from the estate.

\"La famiglia della moneta\", dice quand.easy: "The family of the coin," he says when he sees you, smiling with his gums. "I wanted you to know, before the priest."
\"La famiglia della moneta\", dice quand.short: "The family of the coin. I wanted you to know, before the priest."

\"Proprio voi\", dice quando ti vede, co.easy: "You, of all people," he says when he sees you, almost pleased. "I wanted you to know. So you carry it with you."
\"Proprio voi\", dice quando ti vede, co.short: "You, of all people. I wanted you to know. So you carry it with you."

Per vent'anni, dal 1858 al 1878, Jóska h.easy: For twenty years, from 1858 to 1878, Jóska knocked inside the walls of half the village. Mr Garai paid him, the man with the carnation; Madame had taught him. Gaps in walls, padded hammers, ropes running down to the cellar. The widows wept on the other side of the wall, and he, in the cellar, wept with them, so as not to lose the rhythm.
Per vent'anni, dal 1858 al 1878, Jóska h.short: For twenty years Jóska knocked inside the village walls, paid by Garai. The widows wept, and he wept with them.

\"Ma alla tenuta, mai\", dice, e si aggr.easy: "But at the estate, never," he says, gripping your sleeve. "And the first night, the one in '48, I was six. They were knocking from the big house, and I answered. I was the one who answered. Not the one who knocked."
\"Ma alla tenuta, mai\", dice, e si aggr.short: "But never at the estate. On the first night I was six. I answered. I wasn't the one knocking."

Il notaio arriva in un'ora, con l'inchio.easy: The notary comes within the hour, with ink and two witnesses. Jóska dictates it all, short of breath: the dates, the houses, the payments, the names. He signs with a cross, because he never learned to write, and the cross comes out crooked. The notary seals the confession and gives you a copy.
Il notaio arriva in un'ora, con l'inchio.short: Jóska dictates it all to the notary, and signs with a crooked cross. You have a copy.

Il dottor Lukács, quando la legge, non d.easy: When Dr Lukács reads it, he says nothing for a long moment. Then he shakes your hand, hard, like a man who at last has proof that will stand up in court.
Il dottor Lukács, quando la legge, non d.short: Lukács shakes your hand: at last, proof that will stand up in court.

Il vecchio ti guarda, poi guarda la pare.easy: The old man looks at you, then at the whitewashed ward wall, as if expecting an answer from it. "No one living," he says. "I knew it even as a boy. The living knock with their knuckles. That one knocked with something else."
Il vecchio ti guarda, poi guarda la pare.short: "No one living. The living knock with their knuckles. That one knocked with something else."

Muore quella notte, dicono le suore, sen.easy: He dies that night, the nuns say, without suffering. The nun on duty says that around three she heard slow, regular knocks in the wall behind his bed, and had the feeling that the old man answered before he passed away.
Muore quella notte, dicono le suore, sen.short: He dies that night. The nun hears knocking in the wall, and thinks the old man answers.

Gli tieni la mano. È dura come il cuoio,.easy: You hold his hand. It is hard as leather, covered in burn scars, and at the end it grows light. The old smith falls asleep in the middle of a sentence, his mouth open, and never wakes.
Gli tieni la mano. È dura come il cuoio,.short: You hold his hand. He falls asleep mid-sentence, and never wakes.

Al funerale, il giorno dopo, ci sono sol.easy: At the funeral the next day there are only a nun, an errand boy and you. As the gravedigger lowers the coffin, three soft knocks come from inside, one, two, one: the child's game. The gravedigger crosses himself and says it is the earth settling.
Al funerale, il giorno dopo, ci sono sol.short: At the funeral, three knocks come from the coffin: one, two, one. The child's game.

Il Chemist della piazza ha le vetrine pi.easy: The Chemist on the square has windows full of coloured bottles, a brass scale and a poisons register, as the law demands: anyone who buys arsenic, strychnine or white phosphorus must sign, with their name and the reason for buying. The chemist is a fussy, chatty man, and keeps the register like a prayer book.
Il Chemist della piazza ha le vetrine pi.short: The chemist keeps a poisons register: anyone buying arsenic or phosphorus must sign.

Te lo mostra con orgoglio, sfogliandolo.easy: He shows it to you proudly, leafing backwards. White phosphorus, every month, for thirty years: the Circle's funeral parlour ("to light the chapels"), a Viennese photographer ("for plates"), a certain Mrs Vámos ("for rheumatism"). And, more often than any of them, in handwriting you know, your family's estate: "for experiments".
Te lo mostra con orgoglio, sfogliandolo.short: White phosphorus for thirty years: the Circle's funeral parlour, a photographer, Mrs Vámos. And, most of all, your family.

Il farmacista non vuole venderlo: è un d.easy: The chemist will not sell it: it is a legal document. Then he sees how much you are offering, and decides that the law, after all, only says the register must exist, not where. You leave with it under your arm, wrapped in brown paper.
Il farmacista non vuole venderlo: è un d.short: The chemist will not sell it. Then he sees what you offer, and changes his mind.

A casa lo leggi tutto. Il Circolo ha com.easy: At home you read it all. The Circle bought enough phosphorus to make every ghost in the province glow. Your family, though, bought twice as much.
A casa lo leggi tutto. Il Circolo ha com.short: The Circle bought a lot of phosphorus. Your family bought twice as much.

Il farmacista pesa la polvere con il cuc.easy: The chemist weighs the powder with an ivory spoon, wraps it and has you sign. You write your name under those of your parents and grandparents, in the same column, under "for experiments". For a moment it is like carrying on a letter someone else began.
Il farmacista pesa la polvere con il cuc.short: You sign below your parents and grandparents, under "for experiments".
