Aspetti che il farmacista vada nel retro.easy: You wait for the chemist to go into the back room, and tear the pages out one by one, slowly, along the binding. There are eleven. You burn them that same evening in the laboratory stove, where the paper, soaked in who knows what, burns with a green flame.
Aspetti che il farmacista vada nel retro.short: You tear out eleven pages and burn them. They burn with a green flame.

Il giorno dopo il farmacista denuncia il.easy: The next day the chemist reports the theft to the gendarmes. The missing pages, he says, were the Circle's. He remembers nothing else.
Il giorno dopo il farmacista denuncia il.short: The chemist reports the theft. But he only remembers the Circle's pages.

La Factory, sulla riva del fiume, non fa.easy: The Factory, on the riverbank, makes nothing: it is the power station of {0}, with two turbines the size of carriages, a red-brick chimney and a very young engineer from Budapest who loves it as one loves a person. He shows you the dynamos, the valves, the wires running off into town.
La Factory, sulla riva del fiume, non fa.short: The Factory is the power station. The young engineer loves it like a person.

Sa della vostra macchina: lo sanno tutti.easy: He knows about your machine: everyone does. "A telegraph that talks to the dead," he says, amused. "The first customer who wouldn't complain about the bills." Then, more seriously: "A machine like that needs clean, steady current. I can run a cable to the estate for you. Or, if you prefer, to the town hall."
Sa della vostra macchina: lo sanno tutti.short: "Your telegraph needs clean current. I can run a cable to the estate, or to the town hall."

I pali arrivano in una settimana, il cav.easy: The poles arrive in a week, the cable in two. On the evening they switch the current on at the estate, every bulb lights at once, and for a moment the house looks like an ocean liner in the night. Then all the lights flicker together, three times: one, two, one. The engineer says it is normal. He says it twice.
I pali arrivano in una settimana, il cav.short: The current reaches the estate. The lights flicker three times: one, two, one. "It's normal," says the engineer. Twice.

Di notte la centrale è una cattedrale: l.easy: At night the power station is a cathedral: the turbines turn in the dark, the work lamps throw long shadows, and the hum of the dynamos gets into your teeth. The engineer shows you, on the meter board, a needle that should not move and that instead, every night between three and four, jerks back and forth, like a finger searching for a letter.
Di notte la centrale è una cattedrale: l.short: At night, a needle in the power station moves by itself, in jerks, like a finger searching for a letter.

\"Ho cambiato il contatore tre volte\",.easy: "I've changed the meter three times," he says. "I thought it was a fault, someone stealing current, a mouse. Then I started writing down the movements." He shows you the notebook. They are letters. And the letters, in a row, spell your family's name.
\"Ho cambiato il contatore tre volte\",.short: The engineer wrote down the movements. They are letters, and they spell your family's name.

Ringrazi l'ingegnere e gli dici che la t.easy: You thank the engineer and tell him the estate has always used oil lamps and always will. He shrugs, as disappointed as a rejected lover. A week later the cable goes to the town hall.
Ringrazi l'ingegnere e gli dici che la t.short: You decline. The cable goes to the town hall.

La tenuta resta l'unica casa buia della.easy: The estate stays the only dark house on the hill. In the evening, from town, people look at it and cross themselves, as in the old days.
La tenuta resta l'unica casa buia della.short: The estate is the only dark house on the hill. From town, people cross themselves.

Nell'ufficio del direttore della Nationa.easy: In the National Bank manager's office, in the manager's armchair, sits a tall, thin, very elegant gentleman with a black carnation in his buttonhole. He introduces himself as Mr Garai, president of the Circle of the Last Hour. He looks no more than fifty. He has the same handwriting, he tells you with amusement, as his father and his grandfather.
Nell'ufficio del direttore della Nationa.short: In the bank manager's chair sits Mr Garai, president of the Circle. He looks about fifty.

Conosce i debiti della tua famiglia fino.easy: He knows your family's debts down to the last penny, and he will pay them all, today. In return he wants one thing: the plans of the Telegraph of the Dead, the three ink drawings made by the founder. "They were meant for us, to begin with," he says. "Your ancestor kept them. We have forgiven him. But we would like them back."
Conosce i debiti della tua famiglia fino.short: He will pay all your debts, in return for the Telegraph plans. "They were meant for us to begin with."

Il signor Garai riceve le tavole con un.easy: Mr Garai takes the drawings with almost religious respect, rolls them up and ties them with black ribbon. The bank manager signs the release of the debts with shaking hands. As you leave, you notice a small extra deposit in your account too, "for seventy years' interest".
Il signor Garai riceve le tavole con un.short: Garai takes the drawings like a relic. There is also a deposit in your account, "for seventy years' interest".

Il signor Garai non insiste. Si alza, si.easy: Mr Garai does not insist. He stands, pulls on his gloves, and wishes you luck with the Telegraph. "You will finish it," he says. "It's in the blood. And when you switch it on, you will be the ones calling us." The door closes by itself behind him. The manager, pale, asks if you would like to renegotiate the mortgage.
Il signor Garai non insiste. Si alza, si.short: "You will finish it. It's in the blood. And when you switch it on, you'll be calling us." The door closes by itself.

Passi tre notti a ricopiare le tavole, i.easy: You spend three nights copying the drawings, slipping in tiny mistakes, a reversed winding, a valve in the wrong place. Mr Garai studies them for a long time, through a monocle, then rolls them up and pays. At the door he turns. "The dead will check," he says, smiling. "They're very fussy." That night, in the laboratory, you find your faulty copies on the desk, corrected in pencil, point by point.
Passi tre notti a ricopiare le tavole, i.short: You give him faulty copies. "The dead will check," says Garai. That night you find them on your desk, corrected in pencil.

Al Builder's Office il vecchio capomastr.easy: At the Builder's Office the old foreman, who built the new shops on the square for "a Budapest company", calls you into his office and shuts the door. He has built many strange things, he says, in forty years of work; but never so many at once.
Al Builder's Office il vecchio capomastr.short: The foreman who built the new shops calls you into his office. He has something to show you.

Ti mostra le piante. Ogni negozio ha una.easy: He shows you the plans. Every shop has an extra room, behind the back room, with no windows and a door hidden in the wallpaper. And from every room a brass tube runs under the street to the Circle's Temple. "For talking to each other," he says. "Like on a ship. But who is talking? And to whom?"
Ti mostra le piante. Ogni negozio ha una.short: Every shop has a hidden room, with a brass tube running to the Circle's Temple. "But who is talking? And to whom?"

Il dottor Lukács stende le piante sul ta.easy: Dr Lukács spreads the plans on his office table, holds them down with four books and studies them in silence, like a general studying a map. "The widows upstairs," he says at last, "and the tubes downstairs. That's how they knew everything." He shakes your hand. "This will stand up in court."
Il dottor Lukács stende le piante sul ta.short: "Widows upstairs, tubes downstairs," says Lukács. "That's how they knew everything. This will stand up in court."

Il signor Garai ti riceve nel suo studio.easy: Mr Garai receives you in his study, looks at the plans without touching them and smiles. "They are worth as much as your silence," he says, and writes a figure on a card. It is a generous figure. The plans go into the Circle's stove, in front of you. The next month the foreman retires, with a new house by the lake.
Il signor Garai ti riceve nel suo studio.short: "They're worth as much as your silence," says Garai, and pays well. The plans go into the stove.

La porta nella tappezzeria del negozio d.easy: The door in the glove shop's wallpaper opens with a push. The hidden room is small and dark, with a chair, a little table and the mouth of a brass tube. You sit down. You put your ear to it. From the tube comes a murmur, many voices at once, like a drawing room full of people; then a single voice, very close, which says your name and asks whether the room is to your liking.
La porta nella tappezzeria del negozio d.short: In the hidden room you put your ear to the tube. A voice says your name, and asks if the room is to your liking.

Tra i documenti che passano di mano in m.easy: Among the documents passing from hand to hand in town is a copy of old Jóska the smith's confession, signed with a crooked cross and witnessed by a notary: twenty years of knocking in walls, paid by the day. Everyone who reads it to the end stops at the last line, the one about the first night, and reads it again.
Tra i documenti che passano di mano in m.short: Jóska's confession goes round the town. Everyone stops at the last line, the one about the first night.

Il farmacista della piazza, intanto, rac.easy: Meanwhile the chemist on the square tells all his customers that his poisons register has suddenly become the most interesting book in town.
Il farmacista della piazza, intanto, rac.short: The chemist tells everyone that his poisons register is the most interesting book in town.

E l'ingegnere della centrale, al caffè,.easy: And the engineer from the power station shows anyone at the café who asks a notebook full of letters written by a needle that should not move.
E l'ingegnere della centrale, al caffè,.short: And the engineer shows everyone the notebook written by the needle that should not move.

Il becchino, adesso, è il figlio del vec.easy: The gravedigger now is the son of old Mihály, the gravedigger before him: a man of fifty, big and quiet like his father, with the same cap. He takes you to the founder's grave, the family's first, where it all began fifty-seven years ago.
Il becchino, adesso, è il figlio del vec.short: The old gravedigger's son takes you to the founder's grave, where it all began fifty-seven years ago.

Il tubo d'ottone è ancora aperto, e into.easy: The brass tube is still open, and around the grave lies a heap of folded notes, some new, some yellow and crumbling: the post of the living for the dead, which no one has ever stopped sending.
Il tubo d'ottone è ancora aperto, e into.short: The tube is still open, surrounded by a heap of notes: the post of the living for the dead.

Il tappo di piombo che chiudeva il tubo.easy: The lead plug that sealed the tube lies on the grass beside the headstone, smooth and shiny as a coin. No one touched it: it came out by itself, says the gravedigger, one summer night, with a pop like a champagne cork.
Il tappo di piombo che chiudeva il tubo.short: The lead plug lies on the grass. It came out by itself one summer night, like a champagne cork.

Sul tubo d'ottone qualcuno ha montato un.easy: Someone has fitted a new silver bell to the brass tube, just like the ones at the Circle's funeral parlour. "He gave them the idea," says the gravedigger, pointing at the headstone. "The first one. The others copied it."
Sul tubo d'ottone qualcuno ha montato un.short: A silver bell sits on the tube, like those at the funeral parlour. "He gave them the idea," says the gravedigger.

La lapide è consumata dalla pioggia, e i.easy: The headstone is worn by the rain, and the name can hardly be read. Beside it, in the grass, is still the hole of the old brass tube, filled with earth.
La lapide è consumata dalla pioggia, e i.short: The headstone is worn. Beside it is still the hole of the old tube, filled with earth.

Il Circolo ha chiesto di trasferire le s.easy: The Circle has asked to move the founder's remains to its Temple, into a black marble crypt. The parish is against it. The gravedigger is waiting for the family to decide.
Il Circolo ha chiesto di trasferire le s.short: The Circle wants to move the founder to its Temple. The parish objects. It is your decision.

Il becchino scava per tutto il pomeriggi.easy: The gravedigger digs all afternoon. When the spade hits wood, he stops and takes off his cap. The lid lifts easily, because the nails are gone.
Il becchino scava per tutto il pomeriggi.short: The gravedigger digs. The coffin lid lifts easily: the nails are gone.

Dentro, il fondatore della vostra famigl.easy: Inside, your family's founder is untouched, like the child from the pond in the family stories: his cheeks faintly pink, his lips parted. In his right hand he grips the bell cord. In his left is a pencil, worn down to the wood. And the bottom of the coffin, beneath him, is covered in tiny writing, which no one manages to read before the gravedigger, trembling, closes it again.
Dentro, il fondatore della vostra famigl.short: The founder is untouched, the bell cord in one hand and a worn-down pencil in the other. The bottom of the coffin is covered in writing.

La traslazione si fa di notte, con le to.easy: The move takes place at night, with torches, the Circle's band and two hundred people in black. The coffin, the bearers say, weighs half what it should. In the Temple they lay it in the crypt, under a slab of black marble with a silver eye, and from that day the Thursday séances are held on top of it.
La traslazione si fa di notte, con le to.short: The founder is moved to the Temple at night. The coffin weighs half what it should. Séances are now held above him.

Rispondi al Circolo che il fondatore res.easy: You tell the Circle that the founder stays where he was laid, and Father Benedek blesses the grave again, with holy water that hisses a little on the brass. The Circle does not reply. But the next morning there is a black carnation on the headstone; and beside it, in the grass, the small prints of a woman's shoes, coming up to the grave and not leaving.
Rispondi al Circolo che il fondatore res.short: The founder stays put. Next morning there is a black carnation on the headstone, and a woman's footprints coming but not going.

Il Sindaco Bódi, nipote del vecchio Bódi.easy: Mayor Bódi, old Bódi's grandson, is a smart young man with a centre parting and a leather diary. He is organising the Great Séance for the last night of the year in the town hall's great hall: two hundred chairs in rings, the electric lights off, a table in the middle. "A historic evening," he says. "The Budapest paper is sending a photographer."
Il Sindaco Bódi, nipote del vecchio Bódi.short: Young Mayor Bódi is organising the Great Séance at the town hall. "A historic evening," he says.

\"Mio nonno diceva che con la vostra fam.easy: "My grandfather said your family was good to do business with," he adds. "My father agreed."
\"Mio nonno diceva che con la vostra fam.short: "My grandfather said you were good to do business with."

\"Mio nonno mi ha lasciato una lettera s.easy: "My grandfather left me a letter about you," he adds, still smiling. "It mentions a receipt. My family has a long memory."
\"Mio nonno mi ha lasciato una lettera s.short: "My grandfather left me a letter about you. It mentions a receipt."

\"Mio nonno stava con il parroco\", aggi.easy: "My grandfather sided with the priest," he adds, "and so did you, it seems. But times change, and the town hall belongs to everyone."
\"Mio nonno stava con il parroco\", aggi.short: "My grandfather sided with the priest, and so did you. But times change."

Sul tavolo c'è la pianta della sala, con.easy: On the table is the seating plan, with names in pencil. At the central table, for now, there are only your family and the Circle. The rest can still be rubbed out.
Sul tavolo c'è la pianta della sala, con.short: At the central table, for now, there are only your family and the Circle.

Il Sindaco cancella e riscrive, con una.easy: The Mayor rubs out and rewrites, pulling a face. Dr Lukács accepts with a three-line note: he will bring his notebook and a pocket lamp. Father Benedek accepts with one line: he will bring holy water. The Circle does not reply, and that is an answer in itself.
Il Sindaco cancella e riscrive, con una.short: Lukács will bring his notebook, Benedek his holy water. The Circle does not reply.

Il Sindaco consegna la pianta della sala.easy: The Mayor gives the seating plan to a tall gentleman with a black carnation in his buttonhole, who has been waiting in the anteroom. The gentleman studies it calmly, moves three names, adds one, and says thank you. On his way out he shakes your hand. It is cold; and he seems to you the same age as the portrait in the Circle's drawing room, painted in 1828.
Il Sindaco consegna la pianta della sala.short: A gentleman with a black carnation arranges the seats. His hand is cold, and he is the age of the 1828 portrait.

Il Sindaco intasca la busta con la natur.easy: The Mayor pockets the envelope with the ease that runs in his family and rubs out all the other names at the central table. "A historic evening," he repeats, "deserves a historic family."
Il Sindaco intasca la busta con la natur.short: The Mayor takes the money and rubs out the other names. "A historic evening deserves a historic family."

Nella Foundry si fondono le campanelle d.easy: At the Foundry they are casting the little silver bells for the Circle's graves, the ones tied to the dead's wrists with a thread. The head founder, a man covered in scars, awkwardly shows you the latest order: a bell for every member of your family, from the founder on, each engraved with name and dates.
Nella Foundry si fondono le campanelle d.short: The Circle has ordered a silver bell for every member of your family, with name and dates.

Le campanelle dei morti sono pronte, in.easy: The bells of the dead are ready, in a row on the counter, with both dates. Those of the living have only a birth date. All except one: the one with the name of **{0}**, which already has the second date as well. *31 December 1905.*
Le campanelle dei morti sono pronte, in.short: Those of the living have only a birth date. Except the one for **{0}**: *31 December 1905.*

Paghi il doppio dell'ordine, e il capo f.easy: You pay double the order, and the head founder throws the bells into the crucible one by one. The silver melts quickly, with a hiss. The last into the fire is the one with the date, and it rings, just once, before it melts. The founder says it is air in the metal. He does not meet your eyes.
Paghi il doppio dell'ordine, e il capo f.short: The bells are melted down. The last, the one with the date, rings once before it melts.

Compri la campanella e la porti a casa n.easy: You buy the bell and take it home in your pocket, wrapped in a handkerchief. **{0}** turns it over in their fingers, then puts it on the bedside table, "to get used to it". At night it sometimes rings by itself, softly. There is never any wind.
Compri la campanella e la porti a casa n.short: You buy the bell. **{0}** keeps it on the bedside table, "to get used to it". At night it sometimes rings by itself.

Esci dalla Foundry senza voltarti. Il ca.easy: You leave the Foundry without looking back. The head founder delivers the bells to the Circle, as agreed, and the Circle hangs them in a row in its Temple, under the founder's portrait. The bells of the dead are silent. The one with the date, say the Thursday widows, rings every night at midnight, and every night a little louder.
Esci dalla Foundry senza voltarti. Il ca.short: The bells go to the Temple. The one with the date rings every midnight, louder each time.

La chiesa è fredda e quasi vuota, con l'.easy: The church is cold and nearly empty, smelling of wax and yesterday's flowers. Father Benedek is putting out the candles before the altar with a long brass snuffer. He sees you, calmly finishes his work and comes to sit beside you in the pew, like an old acquaintance.
La chiesa è fredda e quasi vuota, con l'.short: In church, Father Benedek finishes snuffing the candles and comes to sit beside you.

\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.easy: "Tomorrow evening," he says, "your family will sit in the middle of the hall. I am not asking you not to go. I am asking you to go in peace. I have owed you that since I was twelve."
\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.short: "Tomorrow I won't ask you not to go. I'm asking you to go in peace. I owe you that."

\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.easy: "Tomorrow evening," he says, "your family will sit in the middle of the hall. I don't expect to persuade you to stay at home. But my job is to offer, not to persuade."
\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.short: "I won't persuade you to stay home. But my job is to offer, not to persuade."

\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.easy: "Tomorrow evening," he says, "your family will sit in the middle of the hall. I wanted to see you first. To get to know you, at least."
\"Domani sera\", dice, \"la vostra famig.short: "Tomorrow you will sit in the middle of the hall. I wanted to meet you first."

Ti offre quello che un prete può offrire.easy: He offers you what a priest can offer: a confession, a blessing, a little holy water in a chemist's bottle, like the one Father Anzelm carried fifty years before.
Ti offre quello che un prete può offrire.short: He offers you a confession, a blessing, a little holy water.

Ti inginocchi nel confessionale e parli.easy: You kneel in the confessional and talk for a long time: about the knocking, the voices, the Journal, everything your family has done in three generations. Father Benedek listens without interrupting. At the end he gives you no penance: he only tells you to sleep with the light on tonight. You do, and sleep very well.
Ti inginocchi nel confessionale e parli.short: You confess. Benedek only tells you to sleep with the light on. You do, and sleep very well.

Padre Benedek ci pensa a lungo, guardand.easy: Father Benedek thinks for a long while, looking at the altar. Then he nods. "I'll come," he says. "I'll sit at the back, by the door, with my stole in my pocket. If anything goes wrong, I want someone there to remind people that the living have somewhere else to go too."
Padre Benedek ci pensa a lungo, guardand.short: "I'll come. I'll sit by the door. Someone must remind people that the living have somewhere else to go."

Gli dici di no, con gentilezza: la tua f.easy: You politely say no: your family began this story without the Church's help, and will end it the same way. The priest does not insist. He sees you to the door and, on the threshold, makes a small sign of the cross on your forehead with his thumb, without asking. All night your forehead burns, just a little, as after a day in the sun.
Gli dici di no, con gentilezza: la tua f.short: You decline. Benedek makes a sign of the cross on your forehead. All night it burns, just a little.

Nella Library, sul leggio accanto all'in.easy: In the Library, on the lectern by the door, lies the visitors' book: a huge register bound in green leather, where every reader signs on the day of their visit. The librarian, a stern young woman with a pince-nez, shows it to you because, she says, there is something she would like explained.
Nella Library, sul leggio accanto all'in.short: The librarian shows you the visitors' book: there is something she cannot explain.

Sfoglia all'indietro. Ogni mese, dal 185.easy: She leafs backwards. Every month, since 1850, there is the same signature, thin and elegant: *E. Vámos*. Always the same hand, always the same ink, fifty-five years of first Sundays of the month. The last signature is on the last written line. It is dated tomorrow.
Sfoglia all'indietro. Ogni mese, dal 185.short: Every month since 1850 there is the same signature: *E. Vámos*. The last one is dated tomorrow.

La pagina si strappa con un rumore secco.easy: The page tears with a sharp sound that echoes round the reading room. The librarian holds her breath, then nods, like someone approving surgery. The next day, on the fresh blank page, the same signature is already there, dated the day after.
La pagina si strappa con un rumore secco.short: You tear out the page. The next day the signature is back, dated the following day.

Firmi sotto, con la tua calligrafia, la.easy: You sign underneath, in your own hand, with today's date. The pen scratches. When you look up, below your signature there is another, fresh, that was not there before: a handwriting you know from the Journal, slanting backwards. The date is the same as E. Vámos's.
Firmi sotto, con la tua calligrafia, la.short: You sign too. Below your signature another appears, in the Journal's handwriting, dated tomorrow.

La bibliotecaria sorveglia il libro per.easy: The librarian watches over the book all Sunday, sitting by the lectern with her arms folded. No one signs. At closing time, though, when she looks down, the signature is there: it appeared while she was watching, she says, or perhaps while she blinked. From that day she greets the family with great respect, and a little fear.
La bibliotecaria sorveglia il libro per.short: The librarian watches the book all day. No one signs. At closing time the signature is there.

Al tavolo centrale siedono la famiglia,.easy: At the central table sit the family, the Circle and, as agreed with the Mayor, whoever was meant to sit there. Dr Lukács has his notebook open on his knee. Father Benedek keeps one hand in his pocket, on his stole, and does not take his eyes off anyone.
Al tavolo centrale siedono la famiglia,.short: At the central table sit those who were meant to. Lukács has his notebook open; Benedek watches everyone.

Da qualche parte, fuori dalla sala, nel.easy: Somewhere outside the hall, in the cemetery, one of the silver bells on the graves rings by itself, once, as if to signal the start.
Da qualche parte, fuori dalla sala, nel.short: In the cemetery, a silver bell rings by itself, once, as if to signal the start.

Più tardi, chi era presente giurerà che.easy: Later, those who were there will swear that at the first knocks an empty chair at the central table had already been moved, just slightly, as if by someone arriving late from the cemetery.
Più tardi, chi era presente giurerà che.short: Those present will swear an empty chair had moved, as if for someone arriving late from the cemetery.

Il primo a entrare, quella notte, fu un.easy: The first to come in that night was an old man with a notebook under his arm and a pencil worn down to the wood. He greeted no one. He went straight to the central table, sat in the empty chair and began to write, like someone going back to unfinished work. Behind him came a long line of people we knew from the family portraits.
Il primo a entrare, quella notte, fu un.short: The first to come in was an old man with a notebook and a worn-down pencil. He sat in the empty chair and began to write. Behind him came the family portraits.

Il bambino dello stagno gioca ancora in.easy: The child from the pond still plays in the square with the children of the living. He has been eight for seventy years, and he never loses at hide-and-seek.
Il bambino dello stagno gioca ancora in.short: The child from the pond still plays in the square. He has been eight for seventy years.

Il Circolo dell'Ultima Ora si sciolse in.easy: The Circle of the Last Hour broke up within a week. Mr Garai, the Circle's president, the man with the black carnation, left for Budapest on the morning train; the stationmaster swears that when he got into the carriage his hair was black, and that when the train pulled out, it was a white-haired old man waving from the window. Since then his letters no longer have the same handwriting as his father's.
Il Circolo dell'Ultima Ora si sciolse in.short: The Circle broke up. Garai boarded the train with black hair, and a white-haired old man waved from the window.

Al processo contro il Circolo, la prova.easy: At the Circle's trial, the key evidence was old Jóska the smith's confession, with his crooked cross at the bottom of the page. The judge read it aloud, all of it, to the last line; and at the last line, the one about the first night, he stopped, took off his glasses and called a ten-minute break.
Al processo contro il Circolo, la prova.short: At the trial the judge read Jóska's confession. At the last line, the one about the first night, he called a break.

Il libretto francese, con i tre nomi del.easy: The French booklet, with the three names from 1828, went on show in a display case at the University, next to the hollow-heeled shoes and the gauze mask. The students call it "the birth certificate". No one has ever explained how the founder of our family knew, twenty years ahead, what would knock after his death.
Il libretto francese, con i tre nomi del.short: The French booklet is on show at the University. No one has explained how the founder knew, twenty years ahead, what would knock.

Nell'ultima pagina, prima della frase fi.easy: On the last page, before the final sentence, Father named us all: us, our parents, our grandparents, one by one, with dates of birth and death. Beside each name he wrote a mark, like a schoolmaster. I do not have the courage to tell you what mark he gave me. I will tell you only that beside the last line, the empty one, the one for our children, he wrote: *"We shall see."*
Nell'ultima pagina, prima della frase fi.short: Father gave each of us a mark. Beside the empty line, the one for our children, he wrote: *"We shall see."*

Padre Benedek provò a fermare la folla s.easy: Father Benedek tried to stop the crowd on the road to the estate, in his cassock with his arms spread wide, like an old country priest facing a flood. They pushed him aside, without malice. The next day he came among the ashes to bless what was left, and wept, and was not ashamed to do it in front of everyone.
Padre Benedek provò a fermare la folla s.short: Father Benedek tried to stop the crowd. The next day he wept among the ashes, in front of everyone.

Le nostre carte, quelle che avevamo mura.easy: Our papers, the ones we had bricked up in the sacristy with his, were saved. The fire reached the presbytery and stopped in front of the walnut wardrobe, as if before a closed door.
Le nostre carte, quelle che avevamo mura.short: Our papers, bricked up in the sacristy, were saved. The fire stopped at the walnut wardrobe.

Il signor Garai, l'uomo del garofano ner.easy: Mr Garai, the man with the black carnation who had always led the Circle, handed me the presidency that very night, in a room of the Temple, in front of the 1828 portrait. He took the black carnation from his buttonhole and pinned it on my lapel, with cold hands. "I have worn it since 1828," he said. "Now it is your turn. It is a flower that never wilts." I wear it still. It has never wilted.
Il signor Garai, l'uomo del garofano ner.short: Garai gave me his black carnation. "I have worn it since 1828. Now it's your turn." I wear it still. It has never wilted.

Forse ha trovato, tra le carte, le lette.easy: Perhaps you have found, among the papers, the founder's letters to a certain Eszter, or a French booklet with three names at the bottom of its last page. Then you already know that he and I founded the Circle together, in 1828, with a friend who loved carnations. We promised each other that whoever died first would knock. He died first. I have kept my side of the promise another way.
Forse ha trovato, tra le carte, le lette.short: The founder and I founded the Circle in 1828. We promised that whoever died first would knock. He died first. I kept my promise another way.

Del fondatore della famiglia, le dirò so.easy: About the family's founder, I will tell you only that he was the first to knock, and I was the first to answer. The rest is in the minutes, if you read them carefully.
Del fondatore della famiglia, le dirò so.short: The founder was the first to knock, and I the first to answer. The rest is in the minutes.

Ho chiesto alle ferrovie. L'orario del 1.easy: I wrote to the railways. The 1906 timetable still has the stop at {0}, with an asterisk: *"service suspended due to fog"*. The 1907 timetable no longer has it. The stationmaster at the stop before told me that on autumn evenings the telegraph on the dead line still beats now and then. Always the same rhythm. One, two, one.
Ho chiesto alle ferrovie. L'orario del 1.short: The 1907 timetable no longer lists {0}. But the telegraph on the dead line still beats: one, two, one.

Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.easy: Dr Béla Lukács died in 1911, at eighty-three, in his office at the University, with his notebook open on his knees. He left his museum of fraud to the University, with a separate box, sealed, on which he had written in his own hand: *"Unexplained."* Inside is a sealed envelope from 1855, with a number, forty-seven, and a note: *"The seal had been opened. But I had changed the number myself, that same morning, and told no one."*
Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.short: Lukács died in 1911. In a box marked *"Unexplained"* is the 1855 envelope: *"I had changed the number myself, that same morning, and told no one."*

Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.easy: Dr Béla Lukács died in 1911, at eighty-three. In his memoirs, three volumes full of names, the family from the estate appears only once, in a footnote: *"People who laughed too soon."*
Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.short: Lukács died in 1911. In his memoirs your family appears only once: *"People who laughed too soon."*

Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.easy: Dr Béla Lukács died in 1911, at eighty-three, without ever having seen a ghost, and he was proud of it.
Il dottor Béla Lukács morì nel 1911, a o.short: Lukács died in 1911 without ever seeing a ghost, and he was proud of it.

Padre Benedek morì nel 1919. È a lui, e.easy: Father Benedek died in 1919. It is to him, and to someone from that family, that I owe these crates: their papers were bricked up together with his, behind the walnut wardrobe, in a cupboard whose door is covered on the inside with knuckle marks.
Padre Benedek morì nel 1919. È a lui, e.short: Father Benedek died in 1919. To him and the family I owe these crates, bricked up together behind the walnut wardrobe.

Padre Benedek morì nel 1919. Le carte de.easy: Father Benedek died in 1919. He bricked up the parish papers himself, behind the walnut wardrobe. The family's papers, his diaries say, had stayed in the trunk in the study at the estate. I do not know who brought them here, or when. The mason I questioned swears he never opened that wall again.
Padre Benedek morì nel 1919. Le carte de.short: Benedek bricked up only the parish papers. The family's stayed at the estate. I do not know who brought them here.

La confessione del fabbro Jóska, con la.easy: The confession of Jóska the smith, with his crooked cross, is in the sixth crate, in a folder of its own. On the smith's grave, in the cemetery, someone has carved a little hammer.
La confessione del fabbro Jóska, con la.short: Jóska's confession is in the sixth crate. Someone has carved a little hammer on his grave.

Sulla tomba del fabbro Jóska, al cimiter.easy: On the grave of Jóska the smith, in the cemetery, someone has carved a little hammer and, below it, three notches: one, two, one.
Sulla tomba del fabbro Jóska, al cimiter.short: On Jóska's grave someone has carved a hammer and three notches: one, two, one.

La lapide con l'angelo, quella del figli.easy: The headstone with the angel, the cooper's son's, is still there. Every winter someone leaves a pair of ice skates on it.
La lapide con l'angelo, quella del figli.short: Every winter someone leaves a pair of skates on the angel headstone.

Del figlio del bottaio non c'è tomba. Ci.easy: There is no grave for the cooper's son. There are only, among the family papers, forty pages of anatomical notes, and the last one breaks off in the middle of a word.
Del figlio del bottaio non c'è tomba. Ci.short: There is no grave for the cooper's son. Only forty pages of notes, the last one breaking off mid-word.

Al cimitero, nelle mattine di nebbia, si.easy: In the cemetery, on foggy mornings, children can still be heard playing hide-and-seek. They count to fifty. There is always one too many.
Al cimitero, nelle mattine di nebbia, si.short: On foggy mornings children play hide-and-seek in the cemetery. There is always one too many.

Le prove dei trucchi raccolte dalla fami.easy: The evidence of tricks the family collected over three generations (pedals, threads, receipts, cylinders, registers) fills a whole crate, the fifth, arranged with touching care. It is, in my view, the finest collection of deceptions in Europe. And none of it explains the first night.
Le prove dei trucchi raccolte dalla fami.short: The evidence of tricks fills a whole crate. None of it explains the first night.

Nella quinta cassa c'è qualche prova dei.easy: In the fifth crate there is some evidence of the Circle's tricks: a pedal drawn from memory, a double photograph, a few receipts. They are not enough to explain anything. Perhaps no one in that family really wanted them to be.
Nella quinta cassa c'è qualche prova dei.short: In the fifth crate is some evidence of the tricks. It is not enough to explain anything.

Il Sindaco di {0}, oggi, è ancora un Bód.easy: The Mayor of {0} today is still a Bódi, the fourth. He received me most courteously and asked me, before anything else, whether I had found a certain receipt among the papers.
Il Sindaco di {0}, oggi, è ancora un Bód.short: The Mayor is still a Bódi. He asked me at once whether I had found a certain receipt.

Il Sindaco di {0}, oggi, è ancora un Bód.easy: The Mayor of {0} today is still a Bódi, the fourth. He received me most courteously and offered me a cigar, which I did not smoke.
Il Sindaco di {0}, oggi, è ancora un Bód.short: The Mayor is still a Bódi, the fourth. He offered me a cigar.

Infine, il signor O. Garai, presidente d.easy: Finally, Mr O. Garai, president of the Circle of the Last Hour. Yesterday evening, at my club in Budapest, a tall gentleman with a black carnation in his buttonhole greeted me by name, asked very politely about my studies and asked me to give his regards to the family. The club porter, when asked, says no one came in that evening.
Infine, il signor O. Garai, presidente d.short: Finally, Mr Garai, president of the Circle. Last night at my club a gentleman with a black carnation greeted me by name. The porter swears no one came in.
